# Regulation (EU) No 1321/2014 Reading Notes


# Chunk 01: Cover Regulation (Articles) and Part-M General, Section A Subparts A and B

# Chunk 01: Cover Regulation (Articles 1 to 8) and Part-M General, Section A Subparts A and B

Source: EASA Easy Access Rules for Continuing Airworthiness, Regulation (EU) No 1321/2014. Chunk file `/home/claude/r1321/chunks/01.txt` (593 lines, read in full).

Status legend used below: **IR** = implementing rule (binding), **AMC** = acceptable means of compliance, **GM** = guidance material. The amending regulation or ED Decision that last touched each item is noted where the text gives it, because it matters for the UK comparison (see the UK flags in each section and the summary at the end).

## 2. Obligations

### Article 3: which rule set applies (determines the regime for each aircraft)
- **Part-M (Annex I)** applies by default to Article 1(a) aircraft and components.
- **Part-ML (Annex Vb)** applies to *other than complex motor-powered aircraft* that are:
  - (a) "aeroplanes of 2 730 kg maximum take-off mass or less";
  - (b) "rotorcraft of 1 200 kg maximum take-off mass or less, certified for a maximum of up to 4 occupants";
  - (c) "other ELA2 aircraft".
  - **Exception:** if such an aircraft is listed in the AOC of an air carrier licensed under Reg. 1008/2008, **Part-M applies**.
- **Art. 3(3): to list a Part-ML-eligible aircraft on a licensed air carrier's AOC**, all three are needed: (a) an AMP approved by the competent authority under M.A.302; (b) due maintenance under that AMP performed and certified under 145.A.48 and 145.A.50 (Part-145 CRS); (c) an airworthiness review performed and a **new ARC issued** under M.A.901.
- **Art. 3(4):** an aircraft with a **permit to fly** follows the specific CAW arrangements defined in the permit (Part-21, Reg. 748/2012).
- **Art. 3(5):** AMPs compliant with M.A.302 as applicable **before 24 March 2020** are deemed compliant with M.A.302 or ML.A.302.
- **Art. 3(6):** operators ensure CAW of Article 1(b) aircraft (third-country, dry leased-in) under **Part-T (Annex Va)**.
- **Art. 3(7):** aeroplanes with MTOM "at or below 5 700 kg" fitted with **multiple turboprop engines** (which are CMPA by definition, because they have more than one turboprop) are treated as non-CMPA for M.A.201, M.A.301, M.A.302, M.A.601, M.A.803, 145.A.30, 66.A.5, 66.A.30, 66.A.70, Part-66 Appendices V and VI, CAMO.A.315, CAO.A.010 and Part-CAO Appendix I.

### Article 4: organisation approvals and transitions
- Organisations are approved "upon their request" under Part-145, Part-CAMO or Part-CAO.
- Part-M Subpart F and G approvals could be issued until **24 September 2020** and were valid until **24 March 2022** (now lapsed in the EU).
- JAR-145 approvals valid before **29 November 2003** are deemed Part-145.
- Holders of Subpart F, Subpart G or Part-145 approvals may get a **Form 3-CAO** on request. Privileges are the same, but capped at Part-CAO Section A privileges. Part-CAO-specific findings had to close by **24 March 2022**, otherwise the approval is revoked, limited or suspended.
- Subpart G holders may get an **EASA Form 14** (Part-CAMO) on request. Part-CAMO-specific findings had to close by **24 March 2022**, with the same consequence.
- Certificates and AMP approvals issued under 1321/2014 as applicable before **24 March 2020** are deemed valid.
- Part-145 holders could close findings against requirements introduced by 2021/1963 (management system/SMS) until **2 December 2024**, derogating from 145.B.350(d)(1) and (2). After that date: revoke, limit or suspend.

### Article 5: certifying staff
- Qualified under Part-66, except under M.A.606(h), M.A.607(b), M.A.801(c), M.A.803, ML.A.801(c), ML.A.803, CAO.A.040(b) and (c), 145.A.30(j) and Part-145 Appendix IV.
- Licences without individual type ratings: privileges continue "until the first renewal or change". The licence is then converted under 66.B.125 to the ratings in 66.A.45.
- Component certifying staff: **national law** applies until EU requirements exist. For maintenance organisations outside the EU, the Agency approves the requirements.
- Limited certifying staff authorisations for flight engineers under 145.A.30(j)(3) or (4) issued before **2 December 2022** stay valid until they expire or the maintenance organisation revokes them.

### Article 6: training (Part-147)
- Type courses approved before the OSD minimum syllabus must include the mandatory OSD elements "not later than 18 December 2017 or within two years after the operational suitability data was approved, whichever is the latest".
- Basic training (or part of it) that commenced before **12 June 2024** must be finished, with its examinations, before **12 June 2026**, and the CofRs must also be issued before **12 June 2026**. They are issued under the pre-12 June 2024 rules.
- For a Part-66 licence issued or changed after 12 June 2024, the authority accepts basic knowledge exam status gained under the pre-12 June 2024 rules.

### Article 7a: competent authorities
- If a State has several authorities, their areas (responsibilities, geography) must be clearly defined and coordinated.
- Authority staff must not perform certification or oversight where there is a conflict of interest (family or financial).
- Authority powers: examine records, data and procedures; make copies or extracts; ask for oral explanations on-site; enter premises, operating sites and means of transport; perform audits, investigations, assessments and inspections, **including unannounced ones**; take enforcement measures.

### Article 8: entry into force (mostly historic)
- In force on the 20th day after OJ publication.
- Optional State opt-outs: Part-66 certifying staff for piston non-pressurised aeroplanes of 2000 kg MTOM and below not in CAT until **28 September 2014**; Part-T (Annex Va) for dry leased-in third-country aircraft until **25 August 2017**. States using these must notify the Commission and the Agency.
- 2a: requirements for SPO and non-air-carrier CAT under Reg. 965/2012 applied from **21 April 2017**, with interim application of M.A.201(f), (h), M.A.306(a), M.A.801(c), M.A.803(b) and M.A.901(g) to defined categories.
- 4: the origin of time for the Part-66 time limits (66.A.25, 66.A.30, Appendix III) for items completed before 1149/2011 applied is the date 1149/2011 applied.
- 6: old-format certificates (Part-M Appendix III; Part-147 Appendices II and III) could be issued until **31 December 2015**. Certificates issued before **1 January 2016** stay valid until changed, suspended or revoked.
- 2018/1142: applies from **5 March 2019**. For ELA1 aeroplanes not in CAT, and aircraft other than aeroplanes and helicopters, Part-66 licence issue applies from **1 October 2019** and the Part-66 certifying staff requirement (M.A.606(g), M.A.801(b)(2), 145.A.30(g),(h)) from **1 October 2020**.

### M.1: competent authority (who oversees what)
1. Individual aircraft CAW oversight and **ARC issue**: the authority of the **State of registry**.
2. Subpart F maintenance organisation: the State of its principal place of business, or the **Agency** if it is in a third country.
3. **AMP approval**: the State of registry, or, if the State of registry agrees before approval, (a) the State of the operator's principal place of business (or its place of establishment or residence if it has none), or (b) the authority overseeing the CAMO managing the aircraft, or the CAMO/CAO holding the owner's **limited contract** under M.A.201(i)(3).
4. Subpart G CAMO: the State of its principal place of business if the approval is not in an AOC; the State of the operator if it is in an AOC; the Agency if it is in a third country.

### M.A.201: responsibilities
- **(a) The owner** is responsible for CAW and shall ensure **no flight** unless all four hold:
  1. the aircraft is maintained in an airworthy condition;
  2. any operational and emergency equipment fitted is correctly installed and serviceable, **or clearly identified as unserviceable**;
  3. the **airworthiness certificate is valid**;
  4. maintenance is performed in accordance with the **AMP (M.A.302)**.
- **(b) Lease:** owner responsibilities transfer to the **lessee** if the lessee is stipulated on the **registration document** or detailed in the **leasing contract**. "Owner" in Part-M means owner or lessee, as applicable.
- **(c)** Any person or organisation performing maintenance is responsible for the tasks performed.
- **(d) Pre-flight inspection:** the responsibility of the PIC, or of the operator for licensed air carriers. It is carried out by the pilot or another qualified person and does **not** need an approved maintenance organisation or certifying staff.
- **(e) Licensed air carrier (1008/2008):** the operator is responsible for CAW and shall (1) ensure the (a) conditions are met; (2) obtain CAMO approval (Part-CAMO, or Subpart G) **as part of its AOC**; (3) hold Part-145 approval, or have a written contract under CAMO.A.315(c) or M.A.708(c) with a Part-145 organisation.
- **(ea) Shared group CAMO (2022/410):** at least two operators in a single air carrier business grouping may use the same CAMO for **all** the aircraft they operate, if: (1) the CAMO is Part-CAMO approved for those aircraft; (2) the CAMO is in the same grouping; (3) there is a contract per **Appendix I to Part-M** between the CAMO and each AOC holder that is not itself a CAMO; (4) the CAMO's principal place of business is in the EU (Treaty territory); (5) the management systems are **harmonised**.
- **(eb)** If an AOC is terminated or revoked and an air carrier no longer meets (ea), it must define and implement an **action plan** acceptable to the authority to comply with (e)(2) "as soon as practicable" (no fixed days).
- **(f) CMPA used for SPO, or CAT other than by licensed air carriers, or by commercial ATOs/DTOs:** the operator ensures the (a) conditions; CAW tasks are performed by a CAMO (Part-CAMO or Subpart G), with an Appendix I written contract if the operator is not itself a CAMO; and the CAMO is Part-145 approved or has a CAMO.A.315(c)/M.A.708(c) contract with Part-145 organisations.
- **(g) CMPA not covered by (e) or (f)** (e.g. private or non-commercial CMPA): the **owner** has the same obligations as (f): a CAMO with an Appendix I contract, and Part-145 maintenance.
- **(h) Non-CMPA used for SPO, or CAT other than by licensed air carriers, or by commercial ATOs/DTOs:** the operator ensures a **CAMO or CAO** (Appendix I contract if the operator is not one). Maintenance by Part-145, Part-M Subpart F, or a CAO with maintenance privileges, or under a written contract with such organisations.
- **(i) Non-CMPA not covered by (e) or (h), or used for limited operations:** the owner ensures the (a) conditions by **one of**: (1) contracting the M.A.301 tasks to a CAMO or CAO via an **Appendix I** contract; (2) doing the tasks **himself**; (3) doing them himself **except** the development and approval processing of the AMP, which a CAMO or CAO performs through a **limited contract** under M.A.302.
- **(j)** The owner or operator grants any person authorised by the competent authority **access** to facilities, aircraft and documents, including subcontracted activities.
- **(k)** An aircraft on an AOC used for non-commercial operations or specialised operations under ORO.GEN.310 or NCO.GEN.104 (Reg. 965/2012): CAW tasks must be done by the AOC holder's CAMO or CAO.

### M.A.202: occurrence reporting
- **Who:** any person or organisation responsible under M.A.201 (without prejudice to Part-145 and Part-CAMO reporting).
- **What:** "any identified condition of an aircraft or component which endangers flight safety".
- **To:** (1) the competent authority of the State of registry and, if different, of the State of the operator; (2) the organisation responsible for the type design or supplemental type design (TC/STC holder).
- **(c)** Where maintenance or the airworthiness review is done under a written contract, the contractor also reports to the **owner and the operator** and, when different, the **CAMO or CAO**.
- **(d) Deadline:** "as soon as possible, but no later than **72 hours** from the moment when the person or organisation identified the condition", unless exceptional circumstances prevent this.
- **(e) Follow-up report:** details of the actions intended to prevent recurrence, "as soon as those actions have been identified", in the form and manner the authority sets.
- **(b)** Reports are made in the manner the authority determines and contain all pertinent information known.

Must record the approving authority. AMPs compliant before 24 March 2020 are grandfathered. |

Per GM2, the operator must assess the CAMO's capability and capacity (Appendix I point 7). |

| **Written maintenance contract CAMO to Part-145** | M.A.201(e)(3), (f)(3), (g)(3); CAMO.A.315(c) / M.A.708(c) | Needed if the CAMO is not itself Part-145 approved. |
| **Written contract CAMO/CAO to maintenance organisation** | M.A.201(h)(3) | With a Part-145, Subpart F or CAO with maintenance privileges. |
| **Air operator certificate (AOC)** | Art. 3(2),(3); M.A.201(e),(k) | Lists the aircraft. A licensed air carrier's CAMO approval is part of the AOC. |
| **Certificate of release to service (CRS)** | Art. 3(3)(b) | Per 145.A.48 and 145.A.50, for due maintenance before AOC listing. |

| **Form 3-CAO** | Art. 4(4) | Part-CAO approval certificate (Appendix I to Part-CAO), converted from Subpart F, Subpart G or Part-145. |
| **Part-145 approval certificate**; legacy **JAR-145** approvals | Art. 4(3), 4(7) | JAR-145 approvals valid before 29 November 2003 are deemed Part-145. |
| **Part-M Subpart F / G approval certificates** | Art. 4(2) | Valid only until 24 March 2022 in the EU. Historical only. |

| **Conversion reports, examination credit reports** | Art. 5(5) | Pre-1149/2011 reports remain compliant. |
| **Limited certifying staff authorisations** (flight engineers) | Art. 5(7) | Issued by the maintenance organisation. Valid until expiry or revocation. |
| **Certificate of recognition (CofR)** (Part-147 training certificates) | Art. 6; GM1 Art. 6(4)/(5) | Basic or type training certificates. Transitional "Part 1" and "Part 2" CofRs carry a mandated note and a list of modules (wording in Section 7). Together they give the same experience reduction (66.B.30(a)) as a normal CofR. |
| **Written contract between Member States** for AMP approval transfer | GM1 M.1(3)(ii) | References the aircraft and the competent authorities, with the terms and conditions of the transfer. |
| **Occurrence report** | M.A.202; AMC M.A.202(b) | Minimum content: reporter or organisation name and approval reference if applicable; identification of the aircraft and/or component; date and time **relative to any life or overhaul limitation** (flying hours, cycles, landings, etc.); details of the occurrence. Sent by any method (electronic, post, fax). Deadline 72 hours. |
| **Follow-up occurrence report** | M.A.202(e) | Preventive actions, in the authority's form and manner. |
| **Action plan** | M.A.201(eb) | Plan acceptable to the authority, after AOC termination breaks (ea) compliance. |
| **Management system harmonisation records**; **group standards** document | AMC1 M.A.201(ea)(b); GM1 M.A.201(ea) | Procedures must specify the records to keep about harmonisation. Group standards may sit in a common document, in each exposition, or in the contract. |
| **Notification by a Member State** of opt-outs | Art. 8(3) | To the Commission and the Agency. |

**Retention periods:** none are stated in this chunk. CAW record retention is in M.A.305 and ML.A.305 (later chunks). Signatories are not specified here, apart from the authority approving the AMP and issuing the ARC, the maintenance organisation issuing limited authorisations, and Part-147 organisations issuing CofRs.

## 4. Defined Terms (Article 2, plus terms with regulatory meaning)

- **Aircraft**: "any machine that can derive support in the atmosphere from the reactions of the air other than reactions of the air against the earth's surface".
- **Certifying staff**: "personnel responsible for the release of an aircraft or a component after maintenance".
- **Component**: "any engine, propeller, part or appliance".
- **Continuing airworthiness**: "all of the processes ensuring that, at any time in its operating life, the aircraft complies with the airworthiness requirements in force and is in a condition for safe operation".
- **JAA** / **JAR**: Joint Aviation Authorities / Joint Aviation Requirements.
- **Commercial air transport (CAT) operation**: "an aircraft operation to transport passengers, cargo or mail for remuneration or other valuable consideration".
- **Maintenance**: "any one or combination of the following activities: overhaul, repair, inspection, replacement, modification or defect rectification of an aircraft or component, with the exception of pre-flight inspection".
- **Organisation**: "a natural person, a legal person or part of a legal person". It may be established at more than one location, inside or outside the Member States. (So a sole trader can be an "organisation".)
- **Pre-flight inspection**: "the inspection carried out before flight to ensure that the aircraft is fit for the intended flight".
- **ELA1 aircraft** (manned European light aircraft):
  - aeroplane, MTOM 1 200 kg or less, not CMPA;
  - sailplane or powered sailplane of 1 200 kg MTOM or less;
  - balloon with design volume of not more than 3 400 m3 (hot air), 1 050 m3 (gas), 300 m3 (tethered gas);
  - airship for not more than 4 occupants, volume of not more than 3 400 m3 (hot air) or 1 000 m3 (gas).
- **ELA2 aircraft**:
  - aeroplane, MTOM 2 000 kg or less, not CMPA;
  - sailplane or powered sailplane of 2 000 kg MTOM or less;
  - any balloon;
  - hot air ship;
  - gas airship with 3 % maximum static heaviness, non-vectored thrust (except reverse), conventional simple structure, control and ballonet design, and non-power-assisted controls;
  - Very Light Rotorcraft.
- **LSA aircraft**: a light sport aeroplane with all of:
  - MTOM not more than 600 kg;
  - VS0 not more than 45 knots CAS at maximum certificated take-off mass and most critical CG;
  - not more than 2 seats including the pilot;
  - a single non-turbine engine with a propeller;
  - a non-pressurised cabin.
- **Principal place of business**: "the head office or the registered office of the undertaking within which the principal financial functions and operational control of the activities referred to in this Regulation are exercised".
- **Critical maintenance task**: "a maintenance task that involves the assembly or any disturbance of a system or any part on an aircraft, engine or propeller that, if an error occurred during its performance, could directly endanger the flight safety".
- **Commercial specialised operations**: operations subject to Part-ORO Subpart SPO (Annex III, Reg. 965/2012).
- **Limited operations** (non-CMPA only):
  - (i) cost-shared flights by private individuals, with the direct cost shared by all occupants including the pilot, and at most **six** persons sharing;
  - (ii) competition flights or flying displays, with remuneration limited to direct cost recovery plus a proportionate share of annual costs, and prizes up to a value set by the authority;
  - (iii) introductory flights, parachute dropping, sailplane towing or aerobatic flights by an ATO (Reg. 1178/2011) with its principal place of business in a Member State, or by an aerial sport or leisure organisation, where the aircraft is owned or dry leased, the flights generate no profit distributed outside the organisation, and flights with non-members are only a marginal activity.
  - Limited operations are **not** CAT or commercial specialised operations.
- **Introductory flight**, **competition flight**, **flying display**: as defined in Article 2(9), (10), (11) of Reg. 965/2012.
- **Management systems harmonisation**: "the coordinated process by which the management systems of two or more organisations interact and share information and methods to reach common or consistent safety and compliance monitoring objectives".
- **Complex motor-powered aircraft (CMPA)**:
  - (i) an aeroplane with MTOM exceeding **5 700 kg**, or certificated for more than **19** passenger seats, or for a minimum crew of at least **two pilots**, or equipped with turbojet engine(s) or **more than one turboprop**;
  - (ii) a helicopter certificated for MTOM exceeding **3 175 kg**, or more than **9** passenger seats, or a minimum crew of at least two pilots;
  - (iii) a **tilt rotor** aircraft.
- **Owner** (M.A.201(b)): the owner or the lessee, as applicable.
- **Single air carrier business grouping** (GM2 M.A.201(ea)): a controlling undertaking and its controlled undertakings, all located in Treaty territory. Control is "dominant influence" through ownership, financial participation, the right to appoint management, governing rules, or other means. The grouping includes 1008/2008 air carriers and one or more Part-CAMO organisations.
- **Competent authority** (AMC M.1): a ministry, NAA or other designated aviation body in the Member State. Only one per area of responsibility.
- **"Light" / "non-Light"** (GM Arts 3 and 4 table): shorthand for aircraft inside or outside the Part-ML scope of Art. 3(2).
- Abbreviations used: AMP, ARC, AOC, CAMO, CAO (combined airworthiness organisation), CAO-CAM (CAO with CAW management privileges), CAO-M (CAO with maintenance privileges), ATO, DTO, SPO, NCO, SRB (safety review board), OSD, CofR, FRMS, TC, STC.

---

## 5. Software Implications

### Aircraft classification engine (core, drives everything else)
- **Aircraft fields:** category (aeroplane, helicopter, other rotorcraft, sailplane, powered sailplane, balloon (hot-air, gas, tethered gas), airship (hot-air, gas), tilt rotor, VLR); MTOM (kg); maximum certificated passenger seating; minimum certificated flight crew; engine type and count (piston, turboprop, turbojet/turbofan); pressurised (y/n); VS0; seats including pilot; balloon or airship envelope volume (m3); occupants (airships); airship characteristics for ELA2 (static heaviness, vectored thrust, power-assisted controls); State of registry; registration mark; permit to fly (y/n); TC or declaration-of-design-compliance holder.
- **Derived flags (computed, with an explanation):** `is_CMPA`, `is_ELA1`, `is_ELA2`, `is_LSA`, `is_multi_turboprop_le_5700kg` (Art. 3(7) special case: CMPA by definition but treated as non-CMPA for listed points).
- **Regime determination:** `regime` is one of Part-M, Part-ML, Part-T, or permit-to-fly arrangements. Rule: Part-ML if non-CMPA AND (aeroplane at or below 2 730 kg, OR rotorcraft at or below 1 200 kg with up to 4 occupants, OR other ELA2) AND not listed on a 1008/2008 air carrier AOC. Otherwise Part-M. Article 1(b) third-country dry lease-in gives Part-T. A permit to fly overrides with "permit conditions". Keep this as versioned, data-driven rules so a UK rule set can differ.
- **Operation type per aircraft (time-bounded):** licensed air carrier CAT; other CAT; commercial SPO; commercial ATO/DTO; non-commercial; limited operations (sub-type: cost-share (at most 6 sharers), competition or display, introductory, parachute, glider tow, aerobatic); AOC aircraft used for NCO or SPO (M.A.201(k)).
- **Responsibility matrix output** (M.A.201(e) to (i) and the GM table): CAMO required? CAO allowed? Self-management allowed? Is Part-145 mandatory, or are Subpart F, CAO-M or independent certifying staff allowed? Show the legal basis (e.g. "M.A.201(h)"). Re-run it whenever the operation type, AOC listing, MTOM, mod status or registration changes.

### Parties and responsibilities
- **Party entity:** owner, lessee, operator (with AOC number and 1008/2008 licence flag), CAMO (Form 14 ref), CAO (Form 3-CAO ref, with CAM and/or M privileges), Part-145 (approval ref), Subpart F (legacy), Part-147, independent certifying staff (Part-66 licence), competent authority, TC/STC holder or design declarant.
- **"Responsible person" resolution:** the owner by default. It transfers to the lessee when (flag) the lessee is on the registration document or (flag) the lease contract says so. The operator for 1008/2008 carriers. Store the evidence document and effective dates.
- **Contract objects:** type is one of Appendix I CAW management contract, limited AMP contract (scope M.A.302(d), (f), (h)), CAMO-to-145 maintenance contract (CAMO.A.315(c) / M.A.708(c)), CAO/CAMO-to-maintenance contract, or group (ea) contract. Fields: parties, aircraft covered, start and end dates, scope, the group management board list (for (ea)), linked group standards document, status (draft, active, terminated). Validation: (ea) needs at least 2 operators, CAMO in the same grouping, EU principal place of business (UK variant to configure), covering all aircraft of each operator, and a harmonisation record.
- **Compliance checks:** for CMPA or commercial cases, block "self-managed" status; require an active CAMO/CAO contract and an appropriate maintenance organisation approval.
- **Competent authority mapping per function (M.1):** the ARC/aircraft oversight authority (State of registry), the AMP approval authority (State of registry, or a transferred one, with a reference to the transfer agreement), and the CAMO or Subpart F oversight authority.

### No-fly gating (M.A.201(a))
An aircraft **airworthy / dispatch status** computed from four inputs:
1. open defects and overdue maintenance (airworthy condition);
2. operational and emergency equipment: each item has a status (serviceable, or unserviceable with "clearly identified" placard confirmed);
3. CofA valid, which in turn depends on ARC validity (later chunk);
4. all maintenance per the **approved current AMP revision**.

Show a red/amber/green status with the reasons. Alert when any input is about to fail.

### AMP record
- Fields: approval method (direct or indirect per M.A.302(c)), approving authority, approval date, revision, grandfathered (pre-24 March 2020) flag, developer (owner, CAMO or CAO via limited contract).

### Pre-flight inspection
- Log it as a separate activity, explicitly **not** maintenance. Performer: PIC or another qualified person. No CRS needed. The responsible party is the PIC, or the operator for air carriers.

### Occurrence reporting workflow (M.A.202)
- **Report object:**
  - reporter (name, organisation, approval reference);
  - aircraft (registration, serial, type) and/or component (P/N, S/N);
  - time-since data at discovery: hours, cycles, landings, and time since overhaul (auto-populate from the tracking data);
  - description, "identified at" timestamp, recipients, submission timestamps, method.
- **Recipient auto-list:**
  - State of registry authority;
  - State of operator authority if different;
  - TC/STC holder or declarant;
  - if under contract: owner, operator, CAMO/CAO.
- **Deadline:** identified_at + **72 h**. Countdown, escalation alerts (e.g. at 24 h and 48 h), and an overdue status with a field to justify "exceptional circumstances".
- **Follow-up report:** linked child record for preventive actions; due "as soon as identified"; prompt after the root cause is closed.
- **Statuses:** draft, submitted (per recipient), follow-up pending, follow-up submitted, closed.
- **Reportability triage prompts (AMC M.A.202(a)):** serious cracks, permanent deformation, burning or serious corrosion of structure found in scheduled maintenance; failure of any emergency system during scheduled testing.
- The organisation must have a nominated occurrence coordinator role with defined authority.
- UK users report via the UK CAA's system (UK MOR). Make the recipient endpoints configurable per jurisdiction.

### Personnel and licences
- **Part-66 licence:** category and sub-category, type ratings or group ratings (66.A.45), technical limitations, legacy JAA origin flag, "conversion due at next renewal or change" flag (Art. 5(4)).
- **Limited authorisations:** e.g. flight engineer (145.A.30(j)(3)/(4)), with expiry and revocation status.
- **Component certifying staff:** qualification basis = national rule (configurable).
- **Training records / CofR:** course type (basic, type), syllabus version (pre- or post-12 June 2024 / 2023/989), part (1 or 2 for transition), list of modules, module mapping per the correlation table (7A/7B become 7; 9A/9B become 9; 11A/11B/11C become 11; 17A/17B become 17; the L modules are renamed). A deadline flag applies to pre-12 June 2024 courses (complete and CofR issued before 12 June 2026). That date is past as of now, so treat it as a validation rule for historic records.

### Organisation approvals
- Fields: approval type (Part-145, Part-CAMO Form 14, Part-CAO Form 3-CAO, Part-147, legacy Subpart F/G, legacy JAR-145), reference, issuing authority, privileges, scope, status (valid, limited, suspended, revoked), transition flags.
- **Findings register:** finding, requirement, deadline, status. Supports transition deadlines (24 March 2022, 2 December 2024) and the consequence (revoke, limit or suspend).
- **Authority access/audit log** (M.A.201(j), Art. 7a): record authority visits, including unannounced inspections, documents provided, and copies taken. Give authority inspectors a read-only role that covers subcontracted activity data.

### Group CAMO module (EU carriers; probably not UK)
- Group, members (AOC holders, CAMO), group management board (accountable managers plus coordinating member), group standards document with versions, harmonisation activities log (joint SRB meetings, exchange of compliance monitoring and oversight results), a common language setting, and an (eb) action plan tracker.

### Permissions (suggested)
- **Owner/lessee:** view everything; approve contracts; self-manage only if the responsibility matrix allows.
- **CAMO/CAO staff:** manage the aircraft under contract (scoped by contract dates and aircraft).
- **Maintenance organisation or certifying staff:** record tasks they performed (M.A.201(c)).
- **Pilot:** pre-flight inspection entry; defect reporting.
- **Authority inspector:** read-only.
- **Occurrence coordinator:** submit reports.

### Rule versioning
Store the applicable regulation amendment per rule (e.g. 2021/700 for Art. 3) and allow parallel EASA and UK rule sets, with effective-date logic for the many transitional dates.

## 7. Notable AMC and GM

- **GM Articles 3 and 4 (applicability matrix):**
  - Non-commercial, non-CMPA "Light" (Part-ML): CAW management by individual, CAO-CAM or CAMO; maintenance by individual certifying staff, CAO-M or Part-145.
  - Non-commercial non-Light non-CMPA: Part-M. Commercial non-CMPA: CAO-CAM or CAMO.
  - All CMPA: Part-CAMO and Part-145 mandatory.
  - Licensed air carrier: always Part-M, Part-CAMO and Part-145 mandatory (Part-ML N/A).
  - Treat this as the product's master "regime and organisation requirement" lookup.
- **GM M.A.201 quick summary table** (non-Part-ML aircraft only):

  | Operation | CMPA | Non-CMPA |
  |---|---|---|
  | Licensed air carrier CAT | CAMO in AOC (unless (ea)) + Part-145 | Same |
  | Other CAT, SPO, commercial ATO | CAMO + Part-145 (M.A.201(f)) | CAMO or CAO + Subpart F / CAO / Part-145 (M.A.201(h)) |
  | Non-commercial, including limited operations | CAMO + Part-145 (M.A.201(g)) | No CAMO/CAO required; maintenance organisation "not always required" (M.A.201(i)) |

- **GM M.A.201(e):** ground de-icing and anti-icing are not Part-145 activities, but the **inspection for fluid residues is maintenance** and needs suitably authorised personnel. The system should classify those tasks as maintenance requiring a CRS or authorisation.
- **AMC M.A.201(e)(2):**
  - A licensed air carrier needs a CAMO approval within its AOC only for the aircraft on its AOC.
  - The airworthiness review privilege is **optional**.
  - There is no independent CAMO approval to manage for air carriers, apart from the (ea) group derogation.
  - The operator remains ultimately accountable.
- **AMC1 M.A.201(ea) harmonisation elements:**
  - a forum sharing SRB results, attended by accountable managers and safety managers (e.g. joint SRB meetings);
  - regular exchange of compliance monitoring and authority oversight results;
  - a common or consistent safety policy and objectives (local extra objectives allowed);
  - common safety management key processes (except organisation-specific ones such as FRMS);
  - cooperation mechanisms for serious concerns, group-level findings, and synchronised changes;
  - procedures describing the interface and the **records to retain**.
- **AMC2 M.A.201(ea):** one common language (e.g. English) for manuals, procedures and communication when aircraft are registered in a State other than the CAMO's, agreed with the authorities.
- **GM1 M.A.201(ea):**
  - group standards endorsed by a group management board (accountable managers plus a coordinating member, possibly a CAMO employee);
  - board names go in, or are referenced from, the contract and are updated on change;
  - the coordinating member's duties are listed;
  - group standards are documented in a common document, in each exposition, or in the contract;
  - they include safety management key processes, identification of the operators and CAMO, board contacts, and change management.
- **GM2 M.A.201(ea):**
  - each organisation stays responsible for its own management system;
  - the air carrier stays **ultimately responsible** for CAW even when it contracts a CAMO, but the responsibility for *performing* the CAW tasks transfers to the CAMO;
  - the operator must still assess the CAMO's capability and capacity (Appendix I point 7).
- **GM3 M.A.201(ea):**
  - Compliant configurations: several AOCs contracting one group CAMO, possibly integrated into another AOC; several CAMOs within one group.
  - Non-compliant configurations: only **one** AOC uses the contracted CAMO; or the CAMO is not contracted for **all** of an AOC's aircraft.
  - Validation rules: at least 2 AOC users per contracted CAMO; full fleet coverage.
- **GM M.A.201(i):** a self-managing owner is fully responsible and should self-assess competence or get expertise. The app could offer a competence self-assessment or acknowledgement step at onboarding.
- **AMC M.A.201(i)(3):** the limited contract covers M.A.302(d), (f) and (h) (AMP development, review and approval processing; details in a later chunk).
- **GM1 M.A.201(k):** using AOC aircraft for NCO or SPO does not relax (f) to (i).
- **GM1 M.1(3)(ii):** AMP approval can move to another State's authority by written State-to-State contract. If it moves to the CAMO's or CAO's authority, the CAMO/CAO's **indirect approval procedure** may be used unless the terms say otherwise.
- **AMC M.1:** only one authority per area of responsibility, even when a State designates several.
- **AMC M.A.202(a):**
  - Report to the **TC holder or the declarant of design compliance**, and liaise with them about service information.
  - Approved organisations must designate a qualified occurrence coordinator with clear authority.
  - Maintenance reportables are "normally limited to" serious structural cracks, permanent deformation, burning or serious corrosion found in scheduled maintenance, and emergency system failures during scheduled testing.
- **AMC M.A.202(b):** any transmission method is acceptable. Minimum content includes **life or overhaul status** (hours, cycles, landings), so occurrence forms should pull time-since figures automatically.
- **GM1 Article 6(4)/(5):** transitional basic training options. Option 1: the whole course on the old syllabus, finished before the end of the transition. Option 2: split into Part 1 (old) and Part 2 (new), within the **same organisation**, with two CofRs carrying the exact notes:
  - Part 1: "This certificate is issued for Part 1 of the basic training course which started before the applicability date of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/989, covering the modules listed below:"
  - Part 2: "This certificate is issued for Part 2 of the basic training course which started after the applicability date of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/989, covering the modules listed below:"
  - Courses finishing after the transition can only use Option 2.
- **GM1 Article 6(6):** old and new modules and levels for the same licence (sub)category are equivalent, and pre-applicability CofRs are equivalent. Merges: 7A/7B into 7, 9A/9B into 9, 11A/11B/11C into 11, 17A/17B into 17. Category L modules were renamed (e.g. 4L "Airframe wooden/metal tube and fabric" became "Wooden and/or metal-tube structure covered with fabric").

## UK flags (guesses, not facts; verify against UK Reg 1321/2014 as retained and amended, and CAA CAP publications)

- **Basic Regulation and terminology:** UK text probably cites the retained Basic Regulation (EU) 2018/1139, not 216/2008. "Member State" and "Agency" are probably replaced by "the CAA" or "the United Kingdom", and "EASA Form" by "CAA Form" (e.g. CAA Form 14 / Form 3-CAO equivalents). EU-territory conditions (e.g. M.A.201(ea)(4), "territory to which the Treaties apply") are probably UK-territory or absent.
- **Amendments after the Brexit transition (from 1 January 2021) may not be in UK law unless the UK made its own equivalents:**
  - 2021/700 (Art. 3 wording; M.A.201(h); Art. 8);
  - 2021/1963 (Art. 4(7) Part-145 SMS findings deadline of 2 December 2024; Art. 5 changes; flight engineer authorisations);
  - 2022/410 (M.A.201(ea)/(eb) business grouping shared CAMO; likely absent in the UK);
  - 2023/989 (Article 2 definitions update; Article 6(4)-(6) basic training transition with the 12 June 2024 and 12 June 2026 dates, and the new Part-66 module structure; the UK may still use the 7A/7B, 9A/9B, 11A-C, 17A/B modules).
  - Also the ED Decisions dated 2022 and 2023 (GM/AMC M.A.201(ea), AMC M.A.202(a) "declarant of design compliance", GM1 Art. 6).
- **Items probably retained:** 2019/1383 and 2020/270 applied during the transition period. Part-ML, Part-CAMO and Part-CAO (24 March 2020 changes) therefore likely exist in UK law, but UK transition dates for Part-CAMO/CAO may have been extended differently. Article 4(2)/(4)/(5) dates such as 24 March 2022 may differ.
- **Part-ML scope wording:** the pre-2021/700 Art. 3(2) text may differ in the UK (e.g. the "not listed in the AOC of a licensed air carrier" proviso).
- **UK-specific light aircraft regimes:** the UK has made or proposed its own changes (e.g. UK Part-ML adjustments, a "light aircraft" ARC/maintenance programme simplification, a Part-66 L licence, and its own Part 21 Light regime). Treat UK limits as configurable.
- **Occurrence reporting:** M.A.202 likely retained, with the UK CAA as the recipient. It interacts with UK Reg 376/2014 (MOR). The 72-hour limit is probably unchanged.
- **Air carrier licensing:** Reg. 1008/2008 is likely replaced by UK operating licence provisions (retained 1008/2008 as UK law).
- **Article 1:** "registered in a Member State" probably becomes "registered in the United Kingdom". Delegation provisions may differ (Art. 83bis arrangements).

# Chunk 02: Part-M Section A Subpart C: Continuing Airworthiness

# Chunk 02: Part-M Section A, Subpart C — Continuing Airworthiness (M.A.301 to M.A.307)

Source: EASA Easy Access Rules for Continuing Airworthiness (Reg. (EU) No 1321/2014), lines 1–432 of chunk 02. Whole chunk read.

Amending instruments quoted against each IR point (useful for UK divergence checks):
- M.A.301: Reg. (EU) 2019/1383
- M.A.302: Reg. (EU) 2023/989
- M.A.303: Reg. (EU) No 1321/2014 (original)
- M.A.304: Reg. (EU) 2022/1360
- M.A.305: Reg. (EU) 2022/1360
- M.A.306: Reg. (EU) 2020/270
- M.A.307: Reg. (EU) 2019/1383

AMC/GM ED Decisions in the chunk: 2015/029/R, 2016/011/R, 2020/002/R, 2022/011/R, 2022/017/R, 2023/013/R.

Note: Part-M applies to aircraft not covered by Part-ML (i.e. in practice complex motor-powered aircraft, aircraft used by licensed air carriers, and other aircraft above Part-ML thresholds). Light GA under Part-ML has its own (simpler) equivalent rules in another chunk.

---

## 1. Scope (IR points)

| Point | Title | One-line plain summary |
|---|---|---|
| M.A.301 | Continuing airworthiness tasks | Lists the tasks (a)–(i) that together ensure continuing airworthiness and serviceability of operational/emergency equipment: pre-flight inspections, defect rectification (with MEL/CDL), AMP maintenance, release per Subpart H, AMP effectiveness analysis (CMPA/air carriers), ADs/ODs/Agency requirements/authority safety measures, mods and repairs per M.A.304, mass and balance statement to PIC/operator, maintenance check flights. |
| M.A.302 | Aircraft maintenance programme (AMP) | Every aircraft maintained to an approved AMP; approval by the competent authority or by indirect approval via a CAMO/CAO; content basis (authority instructions, ICA from DAHs, CS references, Part-26); escalation allowed with review data; reliability programme for CMPA where MSG/condition monitoring; periodic review. |
| M.A.303 | Airworthiness directives | Every applicable AD must be carried out within the AD's requirements, unless the Agency specifies otherwise. |
| M.A.304 | Data for modifications and repairs | Damage must be assessed; mods/repairs must use data approved by the Agency, by a Part 21 DOA, contained in CS requirements (21.A.90B/21.A.431B; 21L.A.62/102/202/222), or declared under Part 21 Light. |
| M.A.305 | Aircraft continuing airworthiness record system | CRS into the record system within 30 days; required contents (dates, in-service life, status of ADs, mods/repairs, AMP compliance, deferrals, LLPs, time-controlled components, mass and balance); retention periods (36 months / superseded / 12 months after permanent withdrawal); clear, correctable entries. |
| M.A.306 | Aircraft technical log system | For CAT, commercial specialised operations (SPO) and commercial ATO/DTO operations: technical log with flight info, current CRS, maintenance statement, outstanding deferred defects, maintenance support guidance; initial issue approved by the competent authority, amendments via CAME/CAE procedures. |
| M.A.307 | Transfer of aircraft continuing airworthiness records | On permanent transfer to another owner/operator, records (and tech log if applicable) must go too; on contracting a CAMO/CAO, records go to it; retention periods continue to apply to the recipient. |

---

## 2. Obligations

### M.A.301 Continuing airworthiness tasks (who: the person/organisation responsible under M.A.201: owner, operator, CAMO or CAO)
Continuing airworthiness and serviceability of operational and emergency equipment "shall be ensured by":
- (a) accomplishment of pre-flight inspections;
- (b) rectification of any defect and damage affecting safe operation, using data per M.A.304 and M.A.401, "taking into account the minimum equipment list ('MEL') and configuration deviation list, when they exist";
- (c) all maintenance per the AMP (M.A.302);
- (d) release of all maintenance per Subpart H (M.A.801 etc.);
- (e) for all complex motor-powered aircraft (CMPA) or aircraft used by air carriers licensed under Reg. (EC) No 1008/2008: analysis of the effectiveness of the approved AMP;
- (f) accomplishment of any applicable: (1) AD; (2) operational directive with a continuing airworthiness impact; (3) continuing airworthiness requirement established by the Agency; (4) measures required by the competent authority in immediate reaction to a safety problem;
- (g) modifications and repairs per M.A.304;
- (h) delivering the mass and balance statement reflecting the current configuration to the pilot-in-command (or to the operator, for licensed air carriers);
- (i) maintenance check flights (MCF), when necessary.

AMC-level obligations:
- Defects affecting safe operation must be rectified within limits prescribed by the approved MEL, CDL or maintenance data; postponement only if agreed by the operator and per a procedure approved by the competent authority (AMC M.A.301(b)).
- Maintenance checks must be performed within AMP limits; postponement only per a procedure agreed by the competent authority (AMC M.A.301(c)).
- Licensed air carriers: CAMO publishes pre-flight inspection guidance; pre-flight personnel training must be demonstrated to the authority; training standard described in the CAME (AMC M.A.301(a) para 3).
- OD incorporation: operator responsible; CAMO assesses airworthiness impact; process set out in an arrangement or common procedure (AMC M.A.301(f)).

### M.A.302 AMP
- (a) Maintenance of each aircraft "shall be organised in accordance with an AMP".
- (b) The AMP and any subsequent amendments approved by the competent authority.
- (c) Indirect approval allowed when continuing airworthiness is managed by a CAMO or CAO, or under a limited contract per M.A.201(i)(3). The indirect approval procedure is part of the CAME (CAMO.A.300 or M.A.704) or the CAE (CAO.A.025), approved by the authority responsible for that CAMO/CAO. Only usable where the CAMO/CAO is overseen by the State of registry, unless a written contract under M.1 point 3 transfers AMP approval responsibility to the CAMO/CAO's authority.
- (d) The AMP must demonstrate compliance with: (1) competent authority instructions; (2) ICA from TC, RTC, STC, major repair design approval, ETSO authorisation holders, declarants of design compliance, or any other Part 21 / Part 21 Light approval holder; CS items per 21.A.90B/21.A.431B; 21L.A.62/102/202/222; (3) applicable provisions of Part-26 (Reg. (EU) 2015/640).
- (e) Derogation: owner/CAMO/CAO may deviate from (d)(2) ICA and propose escalated intervals based on sufficient reviews per (h). "Indirect approval is not permitted for the escalation of safety-related tasks." Additional instructions may also be proposed.
- (f) AMP contains all maintenance, including frequency and tasks linked to type and specificity of operations.
- (g) CMPA with AMP based on MSG logic or condition monitoring: AMP must include a reliability programme.
- (h) Periodic reviews and amendment when necessary, taking into account operating experience, authority instructions, new/modified TC/STC/declarant instructions.
- AMC: review "at least annually"; mandatory Part 21 requirements incorporated "as soon as possible".
- AMC: an aircraft maintained to only one approved AMP at a time; switching may require a transfer check/inspection.
- AMC: escalation of tasks directly approved by the competent authority, except ALIs (Airworthiness Limitation Items), which are approved by the Agency.

### M.A.303 ADs
- Carry out any applicable AD "within the requirements of that airworthiness directive, unless otherwise specified by the Agency."

### M.A.304 Mods and repairs
- Any person or organisation repairing an aircraft or component "shall assess any damage".
- Use only approved/declared data from the five listed sources (a)–(e).

### M.A.305 Records — time limits and retention (exact)
- (a) CRS (per M.A.801 or 145.A.50) entered in the record system "as soon as practicable and no later than 30 days after the completion of any maintenance".
- (e)(1) Technical log: "covering the 36 months period prior to the last entry" (AMC: may be extended if a tech log entry needs longer retention elsewhere in Part-M).
- (e)(2)(i) CRS + detailed records for AD / authority safety measure compliance (aircraft, engines, propellers, components): until superseded by equivalent information "but covering a period not shorter than 36 months".
- (e)(2)(ii) CRS + detailed records demonstrating compliance with M.A.304 data for current mods and repairs (aircraft, engines, propellers, components subject to airworthiness limitations): no end stated, i.e. kept while the mod/repair is current.
- (e)(2)(iii) CRS + detailed records of all scheduled maintenance or other maintenance required for continuing airworthiness: until superseded, not shorter than 36 months.
- (e)(3)(i) In-service history record for each LLP: no end stated (kept for life of part).
- (e)(3)(ii) CRS + detailed records for last scheduled maintenance and subsequent unscheduled maintenance of LLPs and time-controlled components: until superseded by equivalent scheduled maintenance, not shorter than 36 months.
- (e)(3)(iii) ELA2 component fitted without EASA Form 1 per 21.A.307(b)(2): CRS + owner's acceptance statement, not shorter than 36 months.
- (e)(3)(iv) Component fitted without EASA Form 1 per 21L.A.193(b)(2): CRS + owner's acceptance statement, not shorter than 36 months.
- (e)(4) Aircraft permanently withdrawn from service: (b)(1) data (dates, in-service life), last effective (c)/(d) statuses, and most recent CRS(s)/records under (e)(2)(ii) and (e)(3)(i): retained "for at least 12 months".
- (f) Person/organisation responsible under M.A.201 complies with record system requirements and presents records to the competent authority on request.
- (g) Entries "clear and accurate"; corrections made "in a manner that clearly shows the original entry".
- GM interpretation of "superseded ... not shorter than 36 months": for 36 months both old and superseding records are kept; after 36 months only the new one. Task interval < 36 months means more than one set kept; interval > 36 months means only the last set.
- AMC M.A.305(e) IT backup "updated at least within 24 hours of any entry in the primary system".

### M.A.306 Technical log
- Who: operator, for CAT, commercial SPO, commercial ATO or commercial DTO operations.
- Initial issue approved by the competent authority per CAMO.A.105, M.1, or CAO.1(1); amendments managed per CAMO.A.300(c), M.A.704(b)/(c), or CAO.A.025(c) (i.e. via CAME/CAE procedures).

### M.A.307 Transfer
- (a) Transferring owner/operator ensures M.A.305 records (and M.A.306 tech log if applicable) are transferred on permanent transfer.
- (b) Owner contracting a CAMO/CAO ensures M.A.305 records are transferred to it.
- (c) M.A.305(e) retention periods continue to apply to the new owner, operator, CAMO or CAO.
- AMC: dry lease-out of "less than 6 months" generally not a permanent transfer, but records needed for the lease must be transferred to or accessible by the lessee. On termination of operation, records passed to the new owner/operator or stored.
- AMC M.A.305(f): if a maintenance organisation keeps records on behalf of the owner/CAMO, the owner/CAMO remains responsible for retention and for transfer to a new owner/organisation.

### ATL contents (AMC M.A.306(a), 5-section example)
- Section 1: operator registered name and address, aircraft type, complete international registration marks.
- Section 2: when next scheduled maintenance is due (including out-of-phase component changes due before next check); current CRS for the complete aircraft (normally from last check). Flight crew need not get these if next maintenance controlled by other acceptable means.
- Section 3 (sector record): type and registration; date and place of take-off and landing; take-off and landing times; running total of flying hours (to determine hours to next scheduled maintenance); failures/defects/malfunctions affecting airworthiness or safe operation incl. emergency systems and cabin/galley defects affecting safety known to the commander, with commander date and signature, including "nil defect" entries; CRS after rectification identifying the defect(s) or check; fuel and oil uplifted, fuel per tank at start and end of each flight, planned vs actual uplift in same units; de-icing/anti-icing start time, fluid type, mixture ratio; pre-flight inspection signature. Supplementary: time in engine power ranges affecting engine life; number of landings; flight cycles / pressure cycles. Layout: one copy stays on aircraft, one on ground until flight completed; separate after-flight and pre-next-flight parts.
- Abbreviated CRS: "Part-145 release to service" acceptable instead of the full AMC 145.A.50(b) statement, provided the introductory section shows the full statement.
- Section 4 (deferred defects): pre-printed operator name and page serial number; cross-reference to original Section 3 entry; original date of occurrence; brief details; eventual rectification and its CRS or cross-reference.
- Section 5: maintenance support information (how to contact maintenance en route etc.).
- Cabin/galley defects affecting safe operation or occupant safety count as part of the log even if recorded by another means.

## 4. Defined Terms

- **Pre-flight inspection** (AMC M.A.301(a)): "all of the actions necessary to ensure that the aircraft is fit to make the intended flight". Typically: walk-around for condition (wear, damage, leakage) and presence of required/emergency equipment; check of record system/ATL for outstanding deferred defects and that no required maintenance is overdue "or will become due during the flight"; fluids/gases uplifted correct spec, uncontaminated, recorded; doors secure; locks, covers, restraints, blanks removed; surfaces/engines free of ice, snow, sand, dust; de-/anti-icing fluid residue assessment. Oil/hydraulic uplift and tyre inflation may be included, with procedures to detect abnormal consumption.
- **Deferred defects** (AMC M.A.301(b)): "defects reported in operational service which are deferred for later rectification".
- **Carried forward defects**: "defects arising during maintenance which are carried forward for rectification at a later maintenance input".
- **Operational directives with a continuing airworthiness impact**: e.g. ETOPS/LROPS, RVSM, MNPS, AWOPS, RNAV.
- **Other continuing airworthiness requirement established by the Agency**: TC-related requirements such as CMRs, life-limited parts, airworthiness limitations in CS-25 Book 1 Appendix H para H25.4, fuel tank system limitations incl. CDCCL.
- **Maintenance programme** vs **maintenance schedule** (AMC M.A.302): programme includes scheduled tasks, associated procedures and standard maintenance practices; schedule is the scheduled tasks alone.
- **Reliability programme**: means to ensure AMP tasks are effective and periodicity adequate; can escalate, delete, de-escalate or add tasks.
- **Applicable (airworthiness limitation) parameter** (GM M.A.305(b)): flight hours and/or flight cycles and/or landings and/or calendar time and/or any other utilisation unit (AMC also cites APU cycles, engine power range time, pressure cycles).
- **Life-limited part** (GM M.A.305(c)): part the AMP maintenance schedule requires to be permanently removed from service when, or before, the mandatory life limitation (per Reg. 748/2012) is reached in any applicable parameter. Examples: engine HPT disc, landing gear sliding tube.
- **Time-controlled component** (GM M.A.305(e)): component the AMP requires to be periodically removed for workshop maintenance to return it to a specified standard, sub-component replacement, or inspection/test of performance, after a service period controlled at component level per a specified airworthiness limitation. Examples: horizontal stabiliser actuator, landing gear gearbox, ELT functional check, slide/raft batteries, extinguisher cartridges. Under MSG-based AMPs this means Hard Time and On-Condition. A part can be both LLP and time-controlled.
- **Current status** (GM M.A.305(l)): data accurately establishing the level of compliance with a requirement; must identify the item, be dated, and include total in-service life in the applicable parameter at that date. For LLPs: limit, accumulated, remaining.
- **Detailed maintenance records** (GM M.A.305(g)): those the M.A.201 responsible person needs to fulfil Part-M obligations; a subset of what maintenance organisations keep under M.A.614, CAO.A.090(a), 145.A.55(a). Incoming CoCs, batch numbers and individual task card sign-offs need not be kept by the owner/CAMO, but dimensional data may be requested.
- **Airworthiness limitation** (GM M.A.305(h)): "a boundary beyond which an aircraft or a component thereof must not be operated, unless the instruction(s) associated with this airworthiness limitation is (are) complied with."
- **Other maintenance required for continuing airworthiness** (GM M.A.305(i)): unscheduled or out-of-phase maintenance due to abnormal events, e.g. lightning strikes, hard landings, long-term storage, propeller/rotor overspeed, over-torque, main rotor blade impact.
- **In-service history record** (GM M.A.305(j)): records from which LLP current status can be determined (fields above).
- **Permanently withdrawn from service** (GM M.A.305(k)): moving the aircraft or component to a location not used for storage and/or future return to service.
- **Hard Time**: preventive process, actions at periods related to time in service restore the utility margin.
- **On-Condition**: preventive inspection/test at specified periods to decide if it can continue in service.
- **Condition Monitoring**: monitoring a parameter (vibration, temperature, oil consumption) to identify developing faults; may remain in service without preventive maintenance until functional failure.
- **Fly-to-failure**: components outside these processes; corrective maintenance after failure detection.
- **Data equivalent in scope and detail**: logbooks/log cards in the record system.
- **Permanent transfer** (AMC M.A.307(a)): does not generally include dry lease-out under 6 months.
- **Maintenance check flight (MCF)**: defined in the Air Operations Regulation; operated under operator control.
- **Interoperable aircraft technical log system** (GM1 M.A.306(b)): for a CAMO contracted under M.A.201(ea) by operators in a single air carrier business grouping regularly moving aircraft between AOCs; common data formats and data exchange defined.

---

## 5. Software Implications

### Core data objects
- **Aircraft**: registration, type, MSN, operator, owner, operation type (CAT / commercial SPO / commercial ATO / commercial DTO / non-commercial), CMPA flag, licensed air carrier (1008/2008) flag, CAMO/CAO managing, regime (Part-M vs Part-ML), status (active, stored, permanently withdrawn with date). Drives whether ATL, AMP effectiveness analysis, reliability programme and defect-analysis features are mandatory.
- **Utilisation counters** per aircraft, engine, propeller, engine module, APU and component: flight hours, flight cycles, landings, calendar, APU cycles, pressure cycles, time in engine power ranges, custom units. Each status snapshot must be dated with counters at that date.
- **Engine module** records where modular life tracking is used (module-level total life, in-service history, records travel with the module).
- **AMP**: version, approval route (direct authority / indirect via CAME/CAE), approval reference and date, effectivity per registration (one AMP can cover several registrations, with task-level effectivity), preface (inspection standards, permitted tolerances, escalation procedure), basis documents (MRB report, MPD, AMM chapters, component data, Part-26, authority instructions) with revisions, next annual review due date, reliability programme link. Rule: one active AMP per aircraft at a time; changing AMP may need a transfer check.
- **AMP task**: task ref, title, source (MRB/MPD/ICA/CMR/ALI/AD repetitive/mod- or repair-derived/authority/operator additional), MRB cross-reference, control level (aircraft/engine/propeller/component), interval(s) with parameter(s), tolerances, safety-related/ALI flag (blocks indirect approval of escalation; ALI escalation needs Agency approval), escalation history (any change in periodicity or parameter must be recorded).
- **Task compliance record**: last done (CRS date + counters), next due, terminating action flag, linked CRS.
- **AD**: number, revision/amendment, applicability, status (applicable / not applicable with reason / superseded / cancelled), one-time vs repetitive, multi-part steps with method-of-compliance choice, intermediate assessments, last and next for repetitive, due limits in multiple parameters, linked CRS and detailed records, software part numbers.
- **Authority safety measures** (immediate reaction to a safety problem), **operational directives** (ETOPS, RVSM, etc.) and **Agency requirements** (CMR, CDCCL, ALIs): track like ADs.
- **Modification / repair**: data reference and source type (Agency approved / DOA approved / CS-based / Part 21 Light declared), embodied on (aircraft/engine/propeller/component), CRS date, multi-part status, method of compliance, derived AMP tasks, impacts (mass and balance, AFM supplement, ICA). Structural repair fields: description type (doubler, blend, crack, dent), location (stringer/frame refs), dimensions, remaining material for blend-outs; repaired and non-repaired damage.
- **Loadable software part** configuration: P/N tracked independently of hardware where the DAH data identifies it; nav databases and IFE excluded.
- **Component**: P/N, S/N, classification (LLP / time-controlled (hard time / on-condition) / condition monitored / fly-to-failure / LLP + time-controlled), current location (installed on with position, or removed), life limit, accumulated, remaining, since last overhaul/scheduled maintenance, Form 1 reference, owner's acceptance statement (no Form 1 cases), alternate interchangeable part flag (not a mod if DAH published).
- **In-service history entry (LLP)**: date on/off, host type/S/N/weight variant/thrust rating, counters at on/off, events changing life limit or parameter.
- **Defect**: source (in flight / during maintenance), type (deferred vs carried forward), MEL/CDL reference and category limits, deferral procedure reference, raised date, sector cross-reference, rectification CRS, cumulative-effect review flag, crew notification flag. Repetitive and significant flags.
- **CRS**: unique reference, date, counters at release, issuing organisation (Part-145, M Subpart F, CAO, independent certifying staff), scope, linked work items, "certificate after incomplete maintenance" type, abbreviated "Part-145 release to service" variant.
- **Technical log** (for CAT/commercial SPO/ATO/DTO): sector records (date, place and times of take-off/landing, block or flight time, running totals, fuel/oil uplifts planned vs actual, fuel per tank before/after, de-icing start time, fluid type and mix ratio, defects, nil-defect entry, commander signature, pre-flight inspection signature), deferred defect pages with page serial numbers, maintenance statement (next due scheduled and out-of-phase), current CRS, maintenance support info. Approval reference for initial ATL system; amendments via CAME/CAE.
- **Mass and balance report**: current version, linked to mods; delivery record to PIC/operator.
- **Maintenance check flight**: scenario (1 incomplete maintenance + certificate, 2 operator/CAMO choice after CRS, 3 post-troubleshooting confirmation after CRS, 4 permit to fly needed), ATL entry, data to be gathered, appointed crew briefing record, post-flight completion and final CRS.
- **Reliability / effectiveness analysis** (CMPA and air carriers): significant defects, repetitive defects, deferred/carried forward trends, unscheduled removals, system performance; outputs feed AMP amendments.
- **Record transfer**: from/to party, date, scope, lease (dry lease < 6 months not permanent), records accessible to lessee, retention obligations carried over.

### Workflows
- CRS ingestion: alert if a CRS is not entered within 30 days of maintenance completion (configurable warning earlier, hard flag at day 30).
- AD/task forecasting: compute next due per parameter, "whichever first", using utilisation forecasts; show remaining.
- Pre-flight/dispatch check: block or warn if any required maintenance is overdue or "will become due during the flight" (needs planned flight duration/cycles), and show outstanding deferred defects affecting operation.
- Deferral workflow: raise defect, apply MEL/CDL category limit, approval per authority-approved procedure, extension requests, cumulative-effect review, crew notification, closure with CRS.
- Maintenance postponement (task tolerance/extension) per authority-agreed procedure, with audit.
- AMP amendment workflow: draft, review, approval (direct to authority or indirect by CAMO/CAO with eligibility check: CAMO/CAO under State of registry oversight or M.1 point 3 contract; block indirect approval for escalation of safety-related tasks; ALI escalation flagged for Agency approval). Annual review reminder ("at least annually"); prompt to import new DAH ICA revisions and mandatory Part 21 changes "as soon as possible".
- Reliability programme: required flag if CMPA and AMP based on MSG or condition monitoring.
- MCF workflow (four scenarios with differing certificate requirements).
- Record reconstruction workflow for lost/destroyed records, with statement, submission to authority and acceptance status; conservative-method LLP back-to-birth handling with endorsement.
- Aircraft transfer/CAMO change: export full record set in an industry-standard format (e.g. Spec 2000 / ATA style) and printable form; track handover.
- Permanent withdrawal: switch retention clock to "at least 12 months" for specified items.
- Retention engine: per record type, compute earliest deletion date (36 months from last ATL entry; superseded plus 36 months; life of mod/LLP; 12 months after withdrawal). Never purge automatically without review; carry obligations to new holder.

### Integrity, IT and permissions (AMC M.A.305(e) is effectively a spec for the product)
- Search and production of status reports.
- Export to industry-wide data format and/or printing; ability to print a paper version of any retained record.
- Role-based access preventing unauthorised alteration; immutable audit trail with traceability of amendments.
- Corrections must show the original entry (no destructive edits; strike-through/versioning).
- Backup updated within 24 hours of any entry, preferably remote, access-protected.
- Digitised records: store creation date of scan, one record per document, legible (signatures, stamps, dates), authenticity assurance that dates are not changed after creation, retrieval within reasonable time, protection against technological obsolescence.
- Accepted retention formats: original paper or electronic (via approved electronically signed form), paper copy, electronic copy, print of electronic, digitised paper, microfilm/scan. Paper may be disposed of once authority accepts the digitised system.
- Roles: owner, operator, CAMO/CAO staff (planning, records, airworthiness review), maintenance organisation (CRS issuer), certifying staff, PIC/commander (ATL entries, signatures, nil defect, pre-flight signature), pre-flight inspection personnel (training records), authority read access (present records on request).
- Group CAMO serving several AOCs: interoperable ATL and common data formats.

### Alerts
- AD/task/LLP/time-controlled component approaching or past due (per parameter).
- CRS not entered within 30 days.
- Deferred defect approaching MEL/CDL limit; repetitive defect detection.
- AMP annual review due; new DAH revision not yet assessed.
- Mass and balance report not updated after a mod affecting it.
- Records approaching retention end (review, not auto-delete).
- Missing Form 1 for LLP/time-controlled components where required; missing owner's acceptance statement for components fitted without Form 1.

## 7. Notable AMC and GM

- **AMC M.A.301(a)**: pre-flight inspection includes checking that no maintenance will "become due during the flight", which implies forecasting against planned flight duration. De-icing fluid residue may alternatively be controlled by scheduled AMP inspections/cleanings.
- **AMC M.A.301(b)**: for air carriers and CMPA, a continuous defect analysis system covering significant, repetitive, deferred/carried forward defects, and unscheduled removals/system performance. Distinguishes deferred (in service) from carried forward (in maintenance) defects.
- **AMC M.A.301(c)**: owner/CAO/CAMO must have a system to keep checks within AMP limits; postponement only via an authority-agreed procedure.
- **AMC M.A.301(f)**: ODs are the operator's responsibility; CAMO assesses airworthiness impact; process in an arrangement/common procedure.
- **GM M.A.301(i)**: four MCF scenarios determining whether flight is under the CofA (after certificate after incomplete maintenance, or after CRS) or under a permit to fly. Crew may be appointed and briefed by the maintenance organisation to collect in-flight data for the final CRS.
- **AMC M.A.302**: annual AMP review minimum; one AMP at a time; transfer check when changing; preface requirements; repetitive tasks from mods/repairs into AMP.
- **GM M.A.302(a)**: one AMP may cover several registrations with clear task effectivity.
- **AMC M.A.302(d)**: AMP normally based on MRB report/MPD/AMM; MRB cross-reference mandatory where MRB exists; associated reliability/health monitoring is part of the AMP; ALI escalation approved by the Agency, other escalations directly by the competent authority.
- **AMC M.A.302(g)**: reliability programme needed for MSG-based, condition-monitored, or AMPs lacking overhaul periods for all significant components; not needed for non-CMPA or AMPs with overhaul times for all significant components.
- **AMC M.A.304**: options when damage is beyond published data: replacement, TC holder/declarant/Part 21 organisation support, Agency approval.
- **GM M.A.305**: core definitions (LLP, time-controlled, current status, airworthiness limitation, in-service history, permanently withdrawn). Owner/CAMO need not keep incoming CoCs, batch numbers or task card sign-offs.
- **AMC M.A.305(b)1**: modular engine/propeller life tracking; APU cycles where relevant.
- **AMC M.A.305(c)1/2/3**: detailed field-level content of AD, mod/repair and AMP status (key for data model).
- **GM M.A.305(d) and (d)(2)**: tables of which records are needed per component class (LLP, hard time, on-condition, condition monitoring, ELA2 without Form 1). Off-wing maintenance on on-condition items needs the Form 1 kept; condition monitoring items generally do not. DAH-recommended component-level tasks that are not time-controlled need status but no Form 1 retention.
- **AMC M.A.305(e)**: IT system requirements (search, status, export in industry-wide format or print, access control, integrity and amendment traceability), backup within 24 hours, digitised record rules, lost record reconstruction.
- **AMC M.A.305(e)(1)**: 36-month ATL retention may be extended where another Part-M provision requires.
- **AMC M.A.305(e)(2)**: Form 1s and CoCs of parts used in a mod/repair are not substantiation data (kept by the maintenance organisation). Intermediate AD steps form part of the detailed records.
- **GM M.A.305(e)(2)**: worked meaning of "superseded but not shorter than 36 months".
- **AMC M.A.305(e)(3)**: no need for Form 1 for every LLP installation/removal in the history; conservative methods for missing history acceptable if supporting documents are endorsed; consider DAH guidance on reconstruction.
- **AMC M.A.305(f)**: outsourcing record storage does not transfer responsibility.
- **AMC M.A.306(a)**: 5-section ATL model; abbreviated "Part-145 release to service" CRS.
- **AMC M.A.306(b)**: ATL can be paper, computer or mixed; computer systems need safeguards against unauthorised alteration.
- **GM1 M.A.306(b)**: interoperable ATL for group CAMOs.
- **AMC M.A.307(a)**: dry lease under 6 months generally not a permanent transfer.

---

## UK divergence flags (guesses, to verify against UK CAA UK Reg (EU) 1321/2014 and UK AMC/GM)

- References to "the Agency" are likely "the CAA" in UK text; "EASA Form 1" likely "CAA Form 1" (UK accepts EASA Form 1 under conditions); "Member State of registry" likely becomes UK only.
- **Part 21 Light (Annex Ib, Reg. (EU) 2022/1358) and "declaration of design compliance"**: post-Brexit EU material; probably absent from UK M.A.302(d)(2)(iii), M.A.304(d)/(e) and M.A.305(e)(3)(iv). UK may have its own light aircraft design arrangements.
- **M.A.302 (Reg. 2023/989) and M.A.304/M.A.305 (Reg. 2022/1360)** amendments post-date UK exit (31 Dec 2020); the UK text may be the older wording (e.g. older M.A.305 record lists, possibly without the ELA2 Form-1-less component retention item, and different indirect approval wording).
- AMC/GM from ED Decisions 2022/011/R, 2022/017/R and 2023/013/R (GM M.A.305 definitions, LLP/time-controlled tables, MCF GM, interoperable ATL GM) may not be adopted, or may be adopted differently, by UK CAA.
- M.A.201(ea) (group CAMO contracted by multiple AOCs) likely post-Brexit; may not exist in UK.
- Part-CAMO/Part-CAO (Reg. 2019/1383) and M.A.306 (Reg. 2020/270) were in force before exit, so probably retained in the UK.
- MCF definitions in the UK Air Ops Regulation may differ.


# Chunk 03: Part-M Section A Subparts D, E and F: Maintenance Standards, Components, Maintenance Organisation

# Chunk 03 — Part-M Section A, Subparts D, E and F

Source: EASA Easy Access Rules for Continuing Airworthiness (Reg. (EU) No 1321/2014), Annex I (Part-M), Section A:
Subpart D (Maintenance Standards, M.A.401–M.A.403), Subpart E (Components, M.A.501–M.A.504), Subpart F (Maintenance Organisation, M.A.601–M.A.619(b)).
File: /home/claude/r1321/chunks/03.txt (746 lines, read in full). The chunk ends mid-M.A.619 at point (b); M.A.619(c) onwards (handling of findings, timescales) and later points are presumably in chunk 04.

Amending regulations cited in the IR headers: (EU) 2015/1088, 2015/1536, 2018/1142, 2019/1383, 2020/270, 2021/700, 2021/1963, 2022/1360, 2023/989. ED Decisions for AMC/GM: 2015/029/R, 2016/011/R, 2019/009/R, 2020/002/R, 2021/009/R, 2023/013/R.
