### 2.2 Appendix II: Aircraft type practical experience and OJT, list of tasks

**Part 1) Aircraft type practical experience.** Tasks are split into three aircraft categories: A) aeroplanes and helicopters; B) sailplanes and powered sailplanes; C) balloons and airships.

**A. Specific tasks for aeroplanes and helicopters.** These are free-text task lists under about 60 system headings. The headings are:
- Time limits/Maintenance checks
- Dimensions/Areas; Lifting and Shoring; Levelling/Weighing; Towing and Taxiing; Parking and mooring; Placards and Markings; Servicing; Vibration and Noise Analysis
- Air Conditioning; Auto flight; Communications; Electrical Power; Equipment/Furnishings; Fire protection; Flight Controls; Fuel; Hydraulics; Ice and rain protection; Indicating/recording; Landing Gear; Lights; Instruments; Surveillance; Navigation; Oxygen; Pneumatic; Vacuum; Water/Waste
- Central Maintenance System; Airborne Auxiliary power; Structures; Doors; Windows; Wings
- Propeller; Main Rotors; Rotor Drive; Tail Rotors; Tail Rotor Drive; Rotorcraft flight controls
- Power Plant; Piston Engines; Turbine Engines; Fuel and control (piston and turbine); Ignition (piston and turbine); Engine Controls; Engine Indicating; Exhaust (piston and turbine); Oil; Starting; Turbines, piston engines; Engine water injection; Accessory gear boxes; APU

Examples under "Time limits/Maintenance checks":
- "100 hour check (general aviation aircraft)."
- "'B' or 'C' check (transport category aircraft)."
- "Review Aircraft maintenance log for correct completion."
- "Review records for compliance with Airworthiness Directives."
- "Review records for compliance with component life limits."
- Inspection procedures following heavy landing and following lightning strike.

**B. Specific tasks for sailplanes and powered sailplanes.** This is a table with an "x" per task. Its groups are:
- General activities: placards; weighing and W&B sheet; documentation of annual inspection and repair; review records for AD compliance; **"Five annual inspections"**; inspection after an occurrence; dismantling and reinstallation of wings and empennages.
- Levelling/weighing.
- Flight controls: aileron/flaps, elevator and rudder removal, balancing and reinstallation; rudder cable fabrication; elevator pushrod; safeguarding of pins, screws and castellated nuts; sealing of gaps.
- Electrical; avionics (COM, NAV, XPDR, antenna).
- Cabin equipment: belts, oxygen, canopy, pitot/static, instruments, approved equipment, compass compensation, tow release, water ballast, undercarriage, brakes.
- Fuel, engine and propeller: "Refer to the tasks ... in Table A". Also "Verification and adjustment of folding system of powered sailplanes".
- Structures: wooden/metal tube and fabric; composite (laminate, sandwich, partial and complete gel coat); metal (crack testing, riveting, bonding, anti-corrosion).

**C. Specific tasks for balloons and airships.** This is a matrix with the columns Balloon Hot-air | Balloon Gas (free/tethered) | Airship Hot-air | Airship Gas. Some cells say "x (free)" or "x (tethered)". Many tasks carry an "(*)" marker, which this chunk does not explain. Key numeric items:
- "Eight annual inspections (covering at least three different types) (*)" applies to hot-air balloons.
- "Five annual inspections (covering at least two different types) (*)" applies to gas balloons, free.
- "Three annual inspections (covering at least two different types) (*)" applies to gas balloons, tethered, plus one further column. The extracted layout suggests this is the hot-air airship; check against the PDF.
- "Two annual inspections (*)" applies to one column, which the layout suggests is the gas airship; check against the PDF.
- "10-year inspection of fuel cell" applies to two columns: hot-air balloon and hot-air airship.
- Other groups:
  - General activities: functionality test, placards, documentation of annual inspection/repair/ADs/equipment, classification of repair.
  - Weighing and weighing report; envelope fabric strength test; flight control systems (ballonet controls, valves including rip panel); drag rope (free).
  - Electrical; COM/NAV/XPDR; cabin equipment; fire extinguisher; ballast.
  - Envelope (gores, seams, load tapes, deflation system, net, mooring, electrostatic conductivity test "if type is approved for hydrogen", ballonet, suspension cables, catena).
  - Load ring/frame crack detection; heater system (vaporiser, hoses, pilot flame, pressure and leak test, fuel cell disassembly).
  - Basket/gondola; landing gear; wood, composite and metallic structures.
  - Engine, exhaust, propeller, fuel, hydraulic and pneumatic: "Tasks for aeroplanes of comparable certification level".
  - Winch system: "Witness winch inspection" (tethered).

**Part 2) List of tasks for OJT.** The procedure for selecting the minimum task list is:
1. "(i) Filter the ATA chapters (or sub-chapters, when required) applicable to the specific aircraft type (add others if they are missing)."
2. "(ii) Identify relevant and significant tasks for each required category of INS, FOT, SGH, R/I, MEL and TS."
3. "(iii) Retain the required percentage for each task category, and throughout ATA chapters, as much as relevant to the particular aircraft type."

Further rules:
- Tasks that are critical and complex take precedence. The criteria are: difficulty to execute; interpretation of procedures and work instructions; specific tools and equipment; teamwork; human factors (accessibility, HMI); and safety impact on the aircraft and crew.
- "Removal and installation tasks include the final confirmation test, if required."
- "Credit may be given for similar tasks between ATA systems (e.g. pneumatic valves in ATA 21, 30 and 36), but this should be kept to a minimum."
- "Some tasks may be performed on another aircraft type as long as both the system and the task are similar."
- The table is "an acceptable method of selection of OJT tasks for B1 and B2 AML categories ... as required by point 6.2(e) of Appendix III to Annex III."

**OJT task selection table: required percentage of task categories (the same for B1 and B2)**

| Category | INS | FOT | SGH | R/I | MEL | TS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | 75 % | 50 % | 50 % | 50 % | 25 % | 25 % |
| B2 | 75 % | 50 % | 50 % | 50 % | 25 % | 25 % |

Table structure:
- Rows are ATA chapters or sub-chapters. Each row has 12 cells (B1 × 6 categories, then B2 × 6), each marked X or "—".
- Row groups:
  - Introduction subjects: 05, 06, 07, 08, 09, 10, 11, 12, 20 ("Standard practices — only type particular (ATA 50 or 60)").
  - Rotorcraft only: 18, 62-10…62-40, 63-10…63-60, 64, 65, 66, 67.
  - Airframe systems: 21 to 38, 41, 42, 44, 45, 46, 47-00, 50-xx cargo.
  - Airframe structures: 52 to 57.
  - APUs: 49-10…49-90.
  - Turbine engines: 70, 71-xx, 72T, 73 to 80, 83.
  - Piston engines: 70, 71-xx, 72R, 73, 74, 76 to 81, 83.
  - Propellers: 61-10…61-50, 61B, 61C, 61D, 61E.
- Examples:
  - 05 Time limits: B1 INS X; B2 INS X.
  - 24-10 Generator drive: B1 has X in all six categories; B2 is X X — — X X.
  - 22-10 Autopilot: B1 has none; B2 has X in all six.
  - 38-20 Wash: no X at all.
- Some rows have truncated or odd cells in the extraction, for example 71-10 Cowling (turbine). Use the official PDF if exact row data is needed.

**Note for ATA Chapter 5:** "select at least one task from category (a), two tasks from category (b), and three tasks from category (c)":
- (a) Perform or assist in a scheduled check: 100-hour check (GA); daily, weekly, service, transit or equivalent; active participation in an A, B or C check or the equivalent base check.
- (b) Review the aircraft maintenance log for correct completion: closure of MEL/CDL items; dent and buckle chart review per the SRM; fuel or oil leakage tests.
- (c) Unscheduled inspection following one of 26 listed events, including: hard landing, overweight taxiing, bird/hail strike, aborted take-off, high-energy stop, wheel-bearing failure, exceedance of max NLG steering angle, shimmy, lightning/HIRF, tail strike, winglet strike, severe turbulence, airframe vibrations, ice/snow, flight control overspeed, hot-air duct rupture, relief panels open, mercury spillage, galley spill, hydraulic fluid reaction with titanium, cabin overpressure, fuel imbalance, smoke/fumes, abnormal door operation, ferry flight maintenance, and "others".

**GM1 Appendix II.** This is an example OJT list for **B1.1 and B2 (Aeroplanes Turbine)**. It is "not exhaustive, nor tailored to a specific aircraft type, and should be reviewed and adjusted as necessary."
- Columns: `Task No | ATA chapter | Task description | B1.1 | B2`.
- It has **448 numbered tasks**, from Task 1 "05 Perform (assist) in A-Check" (B1.1 X, B2 X) to Task 448 "80 Starting – Troubleshoot faulty system".
- Further examples:
  - Task 3 "Review Dent & Buckle chart": B1.1 only.
  - Task 49 "Perform autopilot gain adjustment": B2 only.
  - Tasks 256–283 (34 Navigation replacements and tests): mostly B2 only.

### 2.3 Appendix III: Evaluation of competence

- **Scope:** "applies to the competence assessment performed by the designated assessors (and their qualifications)."
- **1) What competence means:**
  - It covers three factors: **Knowledge, Skills, Attitude**. Knowledge is normally assessed by examination. This appendix deals with skills and attitude after training that contains practical elements.
  - Evaluation is based on the learning objectives:
    - the (observable) desired performance;
    - the (measurable) performance standard, as tolerances, constraints, limits, rates or qualitative statements;
    - the conditions of the demonstration.
  - Areas of focus:
    - environment awareness;
    - systems integration;
    - areas of special emphasis or novelty (including domains not covered by Part-66 Appendix I and practical elements that simulators cannot teach);
    - using reports and indications;
    - finding and handling aircraft documentation;
    - performing maintenance actions;
    - aircraft final close-up and report, including signing maintenance records and logbooks.
- **2) How to assess:**
  - Use objective, observable criteria linked to the learning objectives and the passing level.
  - Good assessment is "objective, flexible, acceptable, comprehensive, constructive, organised and thoughtful".
  - Suggested questions cover: success factors, criteria, expected expertise, the pass mark ("Go-no go", points or minimum score, "Must know/execute" vs "Good to know" vs "Don't expect ... expert"), minimum or maximum time, how many failures are allowed, and how the trainee is prepared.
  - Assessment type: diagnostic (before the course), formative, or summative (partial or final). It may be done task by task, as a group of tasks, or as a final assessment. Self-assessment followed by discussion is suggested.
  - "A 'box-ticking' exercise would be pointless."
  - The assessor should also consider stress and environmental conditions, test difficulty, evaluation history (progress or sudden poor performance), and the time needed to build competence.
- **3) Who should assess.** The assessor should:
  - be proficient in human performance and safety culture, the aircraft type ("necessary to have the certifying staff privileges in case of CRS issuances"), training/coaching/testing skills, and the instructional tools;
  - understand the objective and content of the practical elements being assessed;
  - have interpersonal skills;
  - "Be ultimately designated by the organisation to carry out the assessment."
- **Combining roles:**
  - The assessor may also be the instructor for the practical elements of type rating training, or the supervisor for OJT. This is allowed provided both roles' objectives are understood and both sets of competence criteria are met.
  - "Whenever possible (depending on the size of the organisation), it is recommended to split the roles (two different persons) in order to avoid any conflicts of interests."

## 3. Records and Documents

No official form (such as an EASA Form) is set out in this chunk. The record formats it implies are:

- **Type rating list entry (Appendix I).** Fields:
  - holder (TC or STC holder, or "WITHOUT TC HOLDER - ORPHANED");
  - model;
  - type of structure (sailplanes and powered sailplanes);
  - Part-66 type rating endorsement text (STCs);
  - note (ELA1/ELA2, tethered, volume in m³, STC number, "(electrical)", "powered variants", series reference);
  - MTOM band (≤2T / >2T).
- **Practical experience record.** Tasks are taken from the Appendix II lists per aircraft category, with counted items such as "Five annual inspections" (sailplanes), "Eight annual inspections (covering at least three different types)" (hot-air balloons), and so on.
- **OJT programme or task list.** Each task needs: task no; ATA chapter or sub-chapter; task description; applicable licence category (B1/B1.1/B2); task category (INS/FOT/SGH/R/I/MEL/TS). The programme should meet the percentage per category, include the ATA 05 minimums (1 from (a), 2 from (b), 3 from (c)), and record any cross-ATA credit or tasks done on another, similar aircraft type.
- **Competence assessment record (Appendix III).** Fields:
  - trainee;
  - assessor, who must be designated by the organisation and hold the required qualifications, including certifying privileges on the type where CRS issue is involved;
  - whether the assessor also acted as instructor or supervisor;
  - assessment type (diagnostic, formative or summative);
  - scope (task, group of tasks, or final);
  - criteria and pass mark;
  - result, number of attempts, and feedback (what was done well, what was done poorly, how to improve);
  - optional trainee self-assessment.
- Maintenance records referenced as content: aircraft maintenance log, AD compliance records, component life-limit records, weight and balance amendment or weighing report, equipment list, MEL/CDL items, dent and buckle chart, annual inspection documentation, and FDR data retrieval.

## 4. Defined Terms

The chunk does not formally define any terms. Terms used, and their meaning in context:

- **ELA1 / ELA2**: European Light Aircraft classes, used as the Note value for Group 4 balloons and airships and for the Group 3 STC entries.
- **Orphaned ("WITHOUT TC HOLDER - ORPHANED")**: a type that no longer has a TC holder.
- **Tethered gas balloon**; **Mixed Gas / Hot-Air Balloons** (Rozière).
- **INS, FOT, SGH, R/I, MEL, TS**: the OJT task categories. They are not expanded in this chunk. They are normally Inspection; Functional/Operational Test; Servicing/Ground Handling; Removal/Installation; MEL (deferral); Troubleshooting. Confirm against Appendix III to Annex III, point 6.2.
- **OJT**: On-the-Job Training.
- **AML**: Aircraft Maintenance Licence.
- **Competence = Knowledge + Skills + Attitude**. "'Attitude' is indivisible from the 'skill'."
- **Assessment types**: diagnostic, formative, summative.
- **Assessor, instructor, supervisor**: three distinct roles that may be combined under conditions.
- Other terms: i.a.w. AMM, SRM, MEL/CDL, HIRF, ESDS, FADEC, CMU, THS, PTU.

## 5. Software Implications

A licence, training or competence feature would need the following.

**Type rating catalogue**
- Import Appendix I as reference data with these fields:
  - `group` (1–4) and `subgroup` (sailplane, powered sailplane, gas balloon, hot-air balloon, gas airship, hot-air airship, Group 3 STC);
  - `holder`, `is_orphaned`, `model`;
  - `structure_type` (enum: metal, composite, wood, metal-tube+wood, mixed);
  - `ela_class` (ELA1/ELA2/none), `tethered` (bool), `envelope_volume_m3`, `mixed_gas_hot_air` (bool), `electric` (bool), `has_powered_variants` (bool);
  - `series_ref` (a range of member models);
  - `stc_number`, `endorsement_text`, `mtom_band`, `source_ed_decision`.
- Use these fields to map a fleet aircraft, plus any embodied STC, to the right AML endorsement.
  - Engine-conversion STCs (Thielert, Technify, SMA, Rotax, Porsche) change the endorsement. The aircraft record should capture embodied STCs.
  - Some STC rows lack an STC number or an MTOM mark, so make those fields nullable.
- **Size:** about 1,550 Group 4 and STC rows in this chunk alone. Import them; do not type them in by hand. Record the ED Decision so the data can be refreshed when EASA revises it.

**Practical experience logbook**
- Store the task templates per aircraft category (A, B, C), with a balloon/airship applicability matrix (hot-air, gas free, gas tethered, hot-air airship, gas airship).
- Support counted requirements with a type-diversity rule, for example 8 annual inspections across at least 3 types for hot-air balloons. A trainee progress engine needs `count_required` and `min_distinct_types`.

**OJT programme builder**
- Inputs: the aircraft type's applicable ATA chapters (a filter, with the option to add chapters); licence category (B1 or B2, with GM1 covering B1.1 and B2).
- The 6 task categories with these percentage targets:

  | INS | FOT | SGH | R/I | MEL | TS |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 75 % | 50 % | 50 % | 50 % | 25 % | 25 % |

- Validation:
  - Check coverage per category against the X-marked cells for each ATA row.
  - Enforce the ATA 05 rule (≥1 from (a), ≥2 from (b), ≥3 from (c)).
  - Flag cross-ATA credit, which should be kept to a minimum.
  - Allow tasks performed on another type, with a justification field.
- Seed the task library from the GM1 448-task list, using ATA, description and B1.1/B2 applicability.
- Each completed task record needs: date, aircraft registration and type, task reference (AMM), category, supervisor, and signature.
- Weight task selection by critical or complex attributes (difficulty, special tools, teamwork, HF, safety impact).

**Competence assessment**
- Assessor register:
  - designation by the organisation (date and scope);
  - qualifications (HF/safety culture, type knowledge, certifying privileges on the type where CRS is involved, instructional skills);
  - role-combination flags (assessor+instructor or assessor+supervisor), with a warning when roles are combined in larger organisations (conflict of interest).
- Assessment record:
  - type (diagnostic, formative or summative) and granularity (task, group or final);
  - criteria tied to learning objectives, pass mark model (go/no-go, points threshold, must-know vs good-to-know);
  - time limits, attempt count and failure policy;
  - self-assessment and assessor comparison;
  - free-text feedback (what went well, what went poorly, how to improve);
  - competency areas from the list of 7 (environment awareness, systems integration, special emphasis, reports and indications, documentation, maintenance actions, close-up and records).
- Avoid a pure checkbox user interface. The guidance says box-ticking is pointless, so support narrative evidence and grouped skills.

**UK context.** UK CAA Part-66 retains equivalent AMC, but its type rating list and ED Decision amendment status may differ from EASA's. Make the catalogue jurisdiction-aware (EASA vs UK CAA source).

## 6. Cross-References

- Appendix I to AMC to Part-66 (list of type ratings): Groups 1–3 are in the earlier chunk. This chunk holds the end of Group 3 (STCs) and all of Group 4.

# PART-147 — Maintenance Training Organisations

## 1. Scope (point by point)

General
- **147.1** Competent authority: Member State-designated authority for organisations with principal place of business in a Member State; EASA for those in a third country. (AMC: may be a ministry/NAA/other body; multiple CAs allowed if one per area of responsibility.)

Section A, Subpart A — General
- **147.A.05 Scope**: requirements for organisations seeking approval to conduct Part-66 training and examination.
- **147.A.10 General**: training organisation must be an organisation (or part of one) registered as a legal entity. (GM: may operate from several addresses and hold several Part approvals.)
- **147.A.15 Application**: application for approval/change on CA form; must include registered name and address, address(es) requiring approval, intended scope/change of scope, accountable manager name and signature, date. (AMC: content per EASA Form 12.)

Subpart B — Organisational requirements
- **147.A.100 Facility requirements**: weather-protected facilities; enclosed separate theory/exam accommodation free from distraction; basic-course workshops/maintenance facilities separate from classrooms (or by written agreement with another organisation, giving CA access); type training access to aircraft type facilities; max 15 students per instructor/assessor in practical training; office accommodation for instructors/examiners/assessors; secure storage for exam/training records; library of technical material; (j) distance-learning derogation from (a)-(d),(f) where organisation has no control of the student's location - must brief student on suitability of location; derogation does not apply to the exam/assessment.
- **147.A.105 Personnel requirements**: accountable manager with corporate authority to finance training; nominated compliance person(s) responsible to AM (may be AM); sufficient contracted staff for training/exams/assessments; other organisation's staff may do practical training/assessment when that organisation provides it; roles of instructor/examiner/assessor may be combined; qualifications per CA-agreed criteria; examiners and assessors specified in exposition; instructors and knowledge examiners updating training at least every 24 months.
- **147.A.110 Records of instructors, examiners and assessors**: maintain records (experience, qualification, training history, subsequent training); terms of reference for all.
- **147.A.115 Instructional equipment**: legible presentation equipment per classroom; virtual training content must be readable/designed for understanding; MSTDs allowed as presentation aids; workshops must have all tools/equipment and an appropriate selection of aircraft, engines, parts, avionics; type training must have access to the aircraft type (MSTDs allowed if adequate standard).
- **147.A.120 Maintenance training material**: course material to students covering Part-66 basic syllabus and/or type course content; access to library examples; may be hard copy or electronic, accessible at any time for the whole course.
- **147.A.125 Records**: keep all student training, examination and assessment records for an **unlimited period**.
- **147.A.130 Training procedures and quality system**: procedures acceptable to CA; quality system with independent audit function (training standards, exam/assessment integrity, procedures) and feedback system of findings to the AM for corrective action.
- **147.A.135 Examinations**: question security; cheating students disqualified and barred 12 months, CA informed within 1 calendar month; examiners supplying answers disqualified, exam void, CA informed within 1 calendar month; exams in a "controlled environment" by the approved organisation, described in the MTOE.
- **147.A.140 Maintenance training organisation exposition (MTOE)**: 12 required content items (see Records section); CA approves MTOE and amendments; minor amendments by indirect approval procedure.
- **147.A.145 Privileges**: basic courses (whole or part), type/task courses, exams of own students, exams of students who did not attend type course, exams of students who did not attend basic course (at approved locations, or elsewhere only via ECQB or CA-selected questions), issue of certificates (Forms 148/149); locations limited to those on certificate or in MTOE, with derogation via MTOE control procedure; subcontracting to non-147 organisations under quality system control, basic limited to Modules 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10; type limited to powerplant and avionics; no exam approval without corresponding training approval, except type examination where type training is not required.
- **147.A.150 Changes**: notify CA of proposed changes affecting approval before they happen; CA may set operating conditions or suspend; failure to notify may result in suspension/revocation backdated to date of change.
- **147.A.155 Continued validity**: unlimited duration, subject to compliance (findings per 147.B.130), CA access, not surrendered/revoked; certificate returned on surrender/revocation.
- **147.A.160 Findings**: level 1 = significant exam non-compliance invalidating exams, refusing CA access after two written requests, no AM, significant training non-compliance; level 2 = any other training non-compliance; holder defines corrective action plan and demonstrates action within CA-agreed period.

Subpart C — Approved basic training course
- **147.A.200 Approved basic training course**: knowledge training + knowledge exam + practical training + practical assessment; knowledge covers Part-66 (sub)category syllabus; exam covers representative cross-section; practical covers tooling, disassembly/assembly, representative maintenance per complete module; assessment checks tool use and working to manuals; duration per Appendix I; hours may be amended (training technology or 66.A.25(e) credits) with justification and MTOE procedure; conversion course durations by syllabus assessment.
- **147.A.205 Basic knowledge examinations**: to Part-66 standard, without training notes, representative cross-section of the module.
- **147.A.210 Basic practical assessment**: by nominated practical assessors at completion of each workshop/maintenance-facility visit period; student must achieve an assessed pass vs 147.A.200(e).

Subpart D — Aircraft type/task training
- **147.A.300 Aircraft type/task training**: approval to conduct Part-66 type and/or task training subject to 66.A.45 standard.
- **147.A.305 Aircraft type evaluation and task assessment**: an organisation approved for type training conducts the Part-66 type evaluation / task assessment to 66.A.45.

Section B — Procedures for competent authorities
- **147.B.05 Scope**: administrative requirements for CAs.
- **147.B.10 Competent authority**: designated CA with documented procedures and structure; adequate staffing; procedures kept current; staff qualified and trained (initial and continuation) in Part-66/Part-147.
- **147.B.20 Record-keeping**: traceable record system; 8 minimum record types; retention minimum 4 years.
- **147.B.25 Exemptions**: CA may exempt a State education department school from legal-entity requirement, from having an AM (senior person with sufficient budget instead), and from independent audit (if an independent schools inspectorate audits at the required frequency); exemptions under Art. 71(1) of 2018/1139 recorded and retained.
- Subpart B intro: requirements to issue/vary approval.
- **147.B.110 Procedure for approval and changes**: CA reviews MTOE and verifies compliance; findings recorded and confirmed in writing; all findings closed before approval issued; reference number on certificate as EASA specifies.
- **147.B.120 Continued validity procedure**: complete audit at intervals not exceeding 24 months, including monitoring at least one training course and one examination; findings per 147.B.130.
- **147.B.125 Approval certificate**: format per Appendix II (EASA Form 11).
- **147.B.130 Findings**: level 1 not rectified within 3 days of written notification -> revocation/suspension/limitation in whole or part; level 2 not rectified within CA-granted timescale -> revoke/limit/suspend.
- **147.B.200 Revocation, suspension, limitation**: suspend on reasonable grounds for potential safety threat; or suspend/revoke/limit per 147.B.130.

Appendices to Annex IV
- **Appendix I**: basic training course minimum durations (table below).
- **Appendix II**: EASA Form 11 approval certificate and schedule.
- **Appendix III**: Certificates of Recognition — EASA Forms 148a/148b (basic) and 149a/149b (type).

Appendices to AMC
- Appendix I: MTOE format; Appendix II: EASA Form 4; Appendix III: EASA Form 22; Appendix IV: EASA Form 12.

## 2. Obligations with exact numbers

| Item | Number | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| Max students per instructor/assessor in practical training | 15 | 147.A.100(f) |
| Instructor and knowledge examiner updating training | at least every 24 months | 147.A.105(h) |
| Typical updating training duration | 35 hours (adjustable); may be split during the 24 months | AMC/GM 147.A.105(h) |
| Organisation size threshold for separate training manager, quality manager, examination manager | capacity >= 50 students at same time (fewer than 50: positions may be combined if CA satisfied) | AMC1 147.A.105 |
| "Large" training organisation (dedicated quality audit group) | >= 50 students; small < 50 | GM 147.A.130(b) |
| Student training/exam/assessment record retention | unlimited | 147.A.125 |
| Internal independent audit covering all Part-147 aspects | at least once every 12 months (single or subdivided per plan) | AMC 147.A.130(b)1 |
| Small organisation contracted audit | twice every 12 months, one unannounced | AMC 147.A.130(b)2 |
| Subcontractor renewal audit | at least once every 12 months, plus pre-audit before use | AMC 147.A.130(b)4 |
| AM review meeting with senior staff (large org) | at least once per year | GM 147.A.130(b)5 |
| Cheating student exam ban | at least 12 months from incident | 147.A.135(b) |
| Notify CA of cheating student / examiner leak | within 1 calendar month | 147.A.135(b),(c) |

| Level 1 finding rectification | within 3 days of written notification | 147.B.130(a) |
| Level 2 finding notice | up to 6 months (initial 3 months to quality manager, final 3 months to AM) | AMC 147.B.130(b) |
| CA full audit interval | not exceeding 24 months; at least 1 course and 1 exam monitored | 147.B.120(a) |
| CA course sampling duration | not less than 3 hours per course; sample 1 basic + 1 type course and their exams | AMC 147.B.120(a) |
| CA written confirmation of non-compliance after audit | within 2 weeks of audit | GM 147.B.110(5) |
| CA oversight record retention | minimum 4 years | 147.B.20(c) |

| Minimum participation for CoR | 90 % of tuition hours, or 95 % content completion for student-centred methods; otherwise no CoR | AMC1 147.A.200(f)2 |

| Subcontractable type training | powerplant and avionic systems only | 147.A.145(d)3 |

**Appendix I — minimum basic course durations**

| Course | Hours | Theory ratio |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | 800 | 30-35 % |
| A2 | 650 | 30-35 % |
| A3 | 800 | 30-35 % |
| A4 | 800 | 30-35 % |
| B1.1 | 2 400 | 50-60 % |
| B1.2 | 2 000 | 50-60 % |
| B1.3 | 2 400 | 50-60 % |
| B1.4 | 2 400 | 50-60 % |
| B2 | 2 400 | 50-60 % |
| B2L | 1 500 + system ratings | 50-60 % |
| B3 | 1 000 | 50-60 % |

B2L system rating additions: COM/NAV +90 h; INSTRUMENTS +55 h; AUTOFLIGHT +80 h; SURVEILLANCE +40 h; AIRFRAME SYSTEMS +100 h (all 50-60 % theory).

**Conversion course typical durations (AMC 147.A.200(g))**
- A1 -> B1.1 or B2: >= 1 600 h; A1 -> B1.1 + B2: >= 2 200 h; 60-70 % knowledge.
- B1.1 -> B2 or B2 -> B1.1: >= 600 h; 80-85 % knowledge.
- B1.2 -> B1.1: >= 400 h; 50-60 % knowledge.
- One A subcategory -> another A: >= 70 h; 30-40 % knowledge.
- Any A -> B2L (any system rating): >= 800 h; 60-70 % knowledge.

Other obligations:
- Accountable manager mandatory (lack of AM = level 1).
- Changes affecting approval notified **before** implementation (147.A.150); name change = new application urgently; AM change notified urgently with exposition statement amendment; senior person change = Form 4; change of location = new application + amended MTOE; additional courses = new application + amended MTOE (basic extensions also need a sample of new exam questions).
- Exams without training notes; questions chosen by examiners; computer or paper based.
- Audit independence: auditors not responsible for the function being audited. Management control/follow-up system must not be contracted out.
- Audit reports raised every audit with target rectification dates.
- Distance learning/CBT: system requirements communicated to user; student activities traceable, documented and recorded; third-party provider written agreement covering delivery, data security, data integrity (AMC1 147.A.115(a)).
- Simulation cannot be the sole training/assessment tool for hand skills (wiring, welding, drilling, filing, wire locking, riveting, bonding).
- Training material: if no amendment service, written warning to that effect.
- Subcontractor contract must give EASA and CA right of access and require the subcontractor to notify changes beforehand.

## 3. Records and Documents

**EASA Form 11 (Issue 6) — Maintenance Training and Examination Organisation Approval Certificate** (Appendix II)
- Page 1: issuing Member State (or EASA), "A Member of the European Union"; Reference `[MEMBER STATE CODE].147.[XXXX]`; company name and address; statement of compliance with Section A of Part-147, approved to provide training, conduct exams per schedule and issue CoRs.
  - Conditions: limited to MTOE scope of work; compliance with MTOE procedures; valid while compliant; unlimited duration unless surrendered, superseded, suspended or revoked.
  - Fields: date of original issue, date of this revision, revision no., signature, for the CA.
- Page 2: Approval Schedule; Reference; Organisation; table of CLASS / LICENCE CATEGORY / LIMITATION:
  - BASIC: B1 (TB1.1 aeroplanes turbine, TB1.2 aeroplanes piston, TB1.3 helicopters turbine, TB1.4 helicopters piston); B2 (TB2 avionics) [B2 basic approval includes B2L for all system ratings]; B2L (TB2L avionics, indicate system rating); B3 (TB3 piston-engine non-pressurised aeroplanes 2 000 kg MTOM and below); A (TA.1 aeroplanes turbine, TA.2 aeroplanes piston, TA.3 helicopters turbine, TA.4 helicopters piston); L (TL, only examination, quote licence subcategory).
  - TYPE/TASK: C (T4), B1 (T1), B2 (T2), A (T3), each "[QUOTE AIRCRAFT TYPE]" with rating and limitation.
  - MTOE reference; date of original issue; date of last revision approved; revision no.; signature.
  - AMC: on page 2, "date of original issue" = original MTOE issue date; "date of last revision approved"/"revision no." = last MTOE revision affecting certificate content; MTOE changes not affecting content do not require reissue.

**EASA Form 148a / 148b — Certificate of Recognition, Basic Training/Examination** (Appendix III.1)
- Used for basic training completion, basic exam, or both. Must identify each module exam by date passed and the corresponding version of Part-66 Appendix I.
- 148a: issued by Part-147 organisation. Reference `[MS CODE].147.[XXXX].[YYYYY]` (org ref + serial). Fields: name; date and place of birth; organisation name/address and org reference; attests attended and/or passed basic course(s) and/or basic exam(s); list of Part-66 modules / location and date of exam passed; date; signature; for company. Cases: attended and passed; attended only; passed exams only.
- 148b: issued by CA after Part-66 Section B Subpart C examination. Reference `[MS CODE].CAA.[XXXX].[YYYYY]`. Fields: name, DoB/place, CA name/address, list of modules/location/date, date, signature.
- AMC examples: full course + all module exams; full course without exams (exams elsewhere -> that organisation issues CoR for exams); all module exams only; certain modules/sub-modules/subjects. "Successful completion of course" = theory + practical training + practical assessment.

**EASA Form 149a / 149b — Certificate of Recognition, Type Training Examination and Assessment** (Appendix III.2)
- Covers theoretical element exam (training included), practical element assessment (training included), or both (Part-66 Appendix III 1(a),(b)); also aircraft type evaluation (66.A.45(d), Part-66 Appendix III point 5).
- Must state airframe/engine combination; course type box: theory only / practical only / both; complete course vs partial (airframe, powerplant, avionic/electrical) vs difference course (e.g. A340 (CFM) for A320 technicians); for partial courses, whether interface areas covered.
- 149a: Part-147 organisation; Reference `[MS].147.[XXXX].[YYYYY]`; fields: name; DoB/place; org name/address/ref; aircraft type training course; start and end dates / location; theoretical/practical elements; or aircraft type evaluation with end date / location; date; signature.
- 149b: CA (exams/evaluations by CA, or direct approval of type training under 66.B.130); Reference `[MS].CAA.[XXXX].[YYYY]`; same fields.
- Cases: attended/passed theory and positively assessed practical; theory only; practical only; type evaluation completed.

**EASA Form 4** (AMC Appendix II) — details of management personnel to be accepted: name, position, qualifications relevant to position, work experience relevant to position, signature/date; CA-use block (accepting staff name, signature, date, office). Required for each 147.A.105(b) nominee except the AM; sent confidentially.

**EASA Form 12** (AMC Appendix IV) — Application for Part-147 initial/change of approval: registered name and address; trading name; addresses requiring approval; tel/fax/email; scope (basic training, type training, using course designators); references to other approvals under the Basic Regulation; AM name, position and signature; date; fee per national legislation.

**EASA Form 22** (AMC Appendix III) — Part-147 Approval Recommendation Report (CA audit report):
- Part 1 General: organisation name, approval reference, requested rating/Form 11 date, other approvals, facility address, audit period, audit dates, audit references, persons interviewed, surveyor, office, signatures, completion date.
- Part 2 Compliance audit review vs 147.A.100, .105, .110, .115, .120, .125, .130, .135, .145, .150, .160, .200, .205, .210, .300, .305; five columns per course/facility/subcontractor; tick / cross with Part 4 finding ref / N/A / N/R.
- Part 3 MTOE compliance against each MTOE item 1.1-4.3; MTOE reference and amendment.
- Part 4 Findings: Part 2/3 ref, audit ref, finding, level, corrective action, date due, date closed, reference. Non-rectified findings copied in writing to the organisation.
- Part 5 Recommendation: scope recommended or continuation of Form 11 scope; applicable Part-147 amendment status; recommending surveyor; date; quality check review.
- AMC 147.B.110(b): record date each finding rectified plus reference document.

**MTOE (AMC Appendix I) structure** — IR 147.A.140(a) 12 items: AM signed statement; nominated persons' titles/names; their duties incl. direct CA liaison; org chart; list of instructors/examiners/assessors; description of facilities at each address; list of courses; amendment procedure; procedures (147.A.130(a)); control procedure for other locations (147.A.145(c)); list of locations (147.A.145(b)); list of subcontractors (147.A.145(d)).
- Part 1 Management 1.1-1.11: corporate commitment; management personnel; duties; org chart; staff list; approved addresses; subcontractors; facilities; courses and type exams approved; change notification; amendment procedure.
- Part 2 Training and examination procedures 2.1-2.18: organisation of courses, course material, classrooms, workshops, conduct of training, training records, storage of training records, training at unlisted locations, organisation of exams, exam security, exam rooms, conduct of exams, practical assessments, marking and records of exams, storage of exam records, exams at unlisted locations, issue of basic course certificates, control of subcontractors.
- Part 3 Quality 3.1-3.8: audit of training, audit of exams, analysis of exam results, remedial action, AM annual review, qualifying instructors, qualifying examiners/assessors, records of qualified staff.
- Part 4 Appendices: forms, syllabi, cross-reference index.
- Format not mandatory if cross-reference index provided and Part 1 items remain in Part 1; Parts 2-4 may be separate manuals with delegated approval (stated in 1.10); combinable with other Part expositions (e.g. Part-145 MOE) with cross-reference index (4.3). CA may approve a delegated exposition approval system for changes not affecting the approval.

**Instructor/examiner/assessor record minimum fields (AMC 147.A.110)**: name; date of birth; personnel number; experience; qualifications; training history before entry; subsequent training; scope of activity; start date of employment/contract; end date if appropriate. Any format; under quality system control; minimal access to prevent unauthorised alteration/disclosure; CA is authorised to inspect. Also record when updating training was scheduled and when it took place (GM 147.A.105(h)). Staff get a copy of their terms of reference.

**CA oversight records (147.B.20(b))**: application; approval certificate incl. changes; audit programme with due and done dates; oversight/audit records; correspondence; exemptions and enforcement; reports from other CAs; exposition and amendments. Retain >= 4 years; secure, controlled access; backups stored at a different location; data accessible through format changes.

**Library contents (AMC1 147.A.100(i))**: relevant EU regulations and national legislation, typical AMMs, SBs, ADs, aircraft and component records, release documentation, procedures manuals, AMPs; large and small aircraft, aeroplanes and helicopters; representative avionics; regularly reviewed/updated.

## 4. Defined Terms

- **Controlled environment** (exams, 147.A.135(d)): environment where identity of students, proper conduct, integrity of the exam and security of exam material can be established and verified.
- **Indirect approval**: approval of minor MTOE amendments via an exposition procedure (147.A.140(c)).
- **Level 1 / Level 2 finding** (147.A.160).
- **Training hour**: 60 minutes of tuition excluding breaks, examination, revision, preparation and aircraft visit (AMC1 147.A.200(f)).
- **Large / small training organisation**: capacity >= 50 / < 50 students.
- **Sub-contract control system**: Part-147 approval temporarily extended to include the subcontractor for the duration; Part-147 org remains responsible.
- **Airframe type training course**: all structure and electrical/mechanical systems excluding powerplant. **Powerplant type training course**: bare engine incl. build-up to QEC unit. Engine/airframe interface covered by either (GA often in airframe). **Avionics/electrical systems type training**: ATA 22, 23, 24, 25, 27, 31, 33, 34, 42, 44, 45, 46, 73, 77 or equivalent (AMC1 147.A.300). Task training may use MBT.
- Training tools (AMC1 147.A.130(a) Table 1, numbered 1-16): slideshow; manuals; computer; mobile devices; videos; **MSTD** (maintenance simulation training device: hardware/software device for training, exam and/or assessment on a component, system or whole aircraft); **mock-up** (scaled/full replica preserving geometric, operational or functional characteristics); virtual reality; **MTD** (maintenance training device, any device other than MSTD, may include mock-ups); **real aircraft** ("suitable" = of the type, or of licence (sub)category with same equipment, for type training; representative for basic; excludes virtual aircraft; "condition" = main components fitted and systems operable); aircraft component; augmented reality; embedded training (e.g. centralised fault display); classroom; virtual classroom (simulated location for synchronous learning); virtual aircraft. **STD** synthetic training devices = generic term covering MSTD, MTD, FSTD.
- Training methods (Table 2): assisted learning (mentoring); CBT (computer-based training, not competency-based); demonstration; distance learning asynchronous / synchronous; e-learning; lecturing; M-learning; multimedia-based training (MBT); simulation; web-based training (WBT). Instructor-centred vs student-centred vs blended training defined.
- Table 3 maps each method to permitted tools and to theory levels 1-3, practical, OJT, and learning objectives (knowledge/skills/attitude), with "limited suitability" marks and "only type"/"type unlimited" notes. Distance learning and M-learning: limited suitability for practical. Instructor involvement should be considered in Module 9 (human factors).
- **ECQB**: European Central Question Bank.
- **Relevant engineering degree** (CA surveyor): aeronautical, mechanical, electrical, electronic, avionic or other relevant studies.

## 5. Software Implications (Airworthiness+)

- **Engineer licensing module**: store CoRs (Form 148a/b, 149a/b) as structured records: CoR reference (`MS.147.XXXX.YYYYY` or `MS.CAA.XXXX.YYYYY`), issuing org ref, holder name/DoB/place, form type, per-module exam pass dates and Part-66 Appendix I version (basic), aircraft type with airframe/engine combination, course scope (theory/practical/both; complete/partial/difference; interface covered), start/end dates, location, type evaluation end date. Use to support Part-66 licence applications/type endorsements and check prerequisites.
- **Validation rules**: B2 basic approval implies B2L all system ratings; basic module subcontracting limited to 1-6, 8-10; type subcontracting limited to powerplant/avionics; exam privilege requires matching training privilege (except type exam where type training not required).
- **Training organisation (MTO) module, if targeted**: Form 11 approval schedule data model (class/category/limitation incl. TB1.1...TA.4, TL, T1-T4 with types); MTOE revision tracking (only revisions affecting certificate content trigger Form 11 reissue); change-notification workflow (pre-approval, Form 4 for nominated persons, new application for location/course additions).
- **Staff records**: instructor/examiner/assessor register with the AMC 147.A.110 fields, terms of reference, 24-month updating-training due date (35 h typical, can be split), schedule vs actual dates. Access control/audit trail (records must not be alterable without authorisation).
- **Student records**: unlimited retention (no auto-delete); attendance tracking with 90 % tuition / 95 % content thresholds before CoR issue; max 6 h theory/day; practical ratio >= 30 % in real maintenance environment; 15:1 practical ratio checks; course hour minima per Appendix I and conversion tables; theory % ranges.
- **Exam integrity**: incident log for cheating (12-month ban date computed, CA notification due within 1 calendar month); examiner disqualification; question bank security; controlled-environment evidence (ID verification, proctoring) for remote/URL exams.
- **Quality/audit module**: 12-month audit plan covering all Part-147 points (Form 22 Part 2 list is a ready-made checklist); small org contracted audits twice per year incl. one unannounced; subcontractor pre-audit and 12-month renewal audit; finding tracker with level, due date, closure date, reference doc; level 1 3-day clock; level 2 up to 6 months (3+3 escalation QM -> AM); annual AM review.
- **Distance learning / LMS integration**: traceable student activity logs, system requirements disclosure, third-party data security/integrity agreements.

# PART-T — Continuing airworthiness of third-country-registered aircraft dry-leased-in by EU air carriers

## 1. Scope (point by point)

- **T.1 Competent authority**: the authority designated by the Member State that issued the operator's AOC oversees the aircraft and organisations.
  - GM T.1: Part-T applies (Art. 1(b), Art. 3(6) of 1321/2014 as amended by 2015/1536) to third-country-registered aircraft whose safety oversight has **not** been delegated to a Member State, when dry leased-in by an air carrier licensed under Reg. (EC) 1008/2008. If oversight has been delegated to a Member State, M.A.201 applies instead (Art. 1(a)(ii)). Dry lease-in approval conditions: ORO.AOC.110.

Section A
- **T.A.101 Scope**: ensures continuing airworthiness of Art. 1(b) aircraft meets Annex V essential requirements of 2018/1139; conditions for persons/organisations managing CAW and maintenance.
- **T.A.201 Responsibilities**: (1) operator responsible for airworthiness and must ensure: (a) type certificate issued or validated by EASA; (b) airworthy condition; (c) valid CofA per ICAO Annex 8; (d) maintenance per a maintenance programme complying with State of Registry requirements and ICAO Annex 6; (e) defects/damage affecting safe operation rectified to State of Registry standard; (f) compliance with State of Registry ADs/continued airworthiness requirements AND EASA mandatory safety information incl. ADs; (g) release to service after maintenance by qualified organisations per State of Registry, signed, with basic details of maintenance; (h) pre-flight inspection before each flight; (i) modifications and repairs comply with State of Registry requirements; (j) records kept (see below). (2) Tasks controlled by the operator's CAMO, which must meet Subpart G. (3) CAMO ensures maintenance and release by a Subpart E maintenance organisation, contracting one if it does not meet Subpart E itself.
- **T.A.501 Maintenance organisation** (Subpart E): CAMO ensures aircraft/components maintained by organisations that: (1) hold a maintenance organisation approval issued or accepted by the State of Registry; (2) scope covers the aircraft/component; (3) have an occurrence reporting system reporting unsafe conditions to the operator, the operator's CA, the TC/STC holder and the CAMO; (4) have an organisation manual describing all procedures.
- **T.A.701 Scope** (Subpart G): requirements additional to Part-CAMO for a CAMO to control T.A.201 tasks.
- **T.A.704 CAME**: in addition to CAMO.A.300, CAME contains procedures for Part-T compliance.
- **T.A.706 Personnel requirements**: in addition to CAMO.A.305, personnel under CAMO.A.305(a)(3)-(a)(5) and (b)(2) need adequate knowledge of the third-country laws of the State of Registry.
- **T.A.708 Continuing airworthiness management**: notwithstanding CAMO.A.315, CAMO must: (a) take aircraft to a maintenance organisation when needed; (b) ensure maintenance per the maintenance programme; (c) apply T.A.201(1)(f) mandatory information; (d) ensure defects corrected by the maintenance organisation per State-of-Registry-acceptable maintenance data; (e) coordinate scheduled maintenance, MSI, LLP replacement and component inspection; (f) manage and archive T.A.201(1)(j) records; (g) ensure mods/repairs approved per State of Registry.
- **T.A.709 Documentation**: notwithstanding CAMO.A.325, hold and use maintenance data acceptable to the State of Registry.
- **T.A.711 Privileges**: Part-CAMO organisation may perform T.A.708 tasks for aircraft on its AOC provided CA-approved procedures exist.
- **T.A.712 Management system**: in addition to CAMO.A.200, ensure compliance with Part-T.
- **T.A.714 Record-keeping**: in addition to CAMO.A.220(a), keep T.A.201(1)(j) records.
- **T.A.715 Continued validity**: in addition to CAMO.A.135, comply with Part-T and grant CA access to facilities, aircraft, documents incl. subcontracted activities.
- **T.A.716 Findings**: after T.B.705 notification: root cause and contributing factors; corrective action plan; demonstrate corrective action - within the CA-set period.

Section B
- **T.B.101 Scope**: CA administrative requirements.
- **T.B.102 Competent authority**: designated CA with documented procedures, structure, adequate staff, qualified/trained staff (initial and continuation), compliance procedures.
- **T.B.104 Record-keeping**: M.B.104(a),(b),(c) apply; per-aircraft minimum records; available on request to other Member State, EASA or State of Registry; retained 4 years after end of dry lease-in.
- **T.B.105 Mutual exchange of information**: M.B.105 applies.
- **T.B.201 Responsibilities**: CA conducts inspections, investigations, aircraft surveys; must inspect before approving the dry lease-in agreement (ARO.OPS.110(a)(1)) to verify T.A.201 compliance; coordinates with State of Registry.
- **T.B.202 Findings**: level 1 = significant non-compliance that lowers safety standard and seriously hazards flight safety; level 2 = non-compliance that could lower safety standard and possibly hazard flight safety; CA takes measures (e.g. grounding) and requires corrective action; level 1 requires corrective action before further flight and notification of the State of Registry.
- **T.B.702 Initial certification procedure**: in addition to CAMO.B.310, CA verifies Part-T procedures and compliance.
- **T.B.704 Continuing oversight**: in addition to CAMO.B.305, CA surveys a relevant sample of Part-T aircraft each oversight planning cycle.
- **T.B.705 Findings and corrective actions**: CA applies CAMO.B.350.

## 2. Obligations with exact numbers

- Aircraft records (T.A.201(1)(j)) available until superseded by equivalent information but **not less than 24 months**.
- Maintenance contract normally for the lease duration, which should **not exceed 7 months** (AMC3 T.A.201(3)); individual work orders acceptable for unscheduled line maintenance and component maintenance up to engines.
- CA per-aircraft oversight records retained **4 years after end of dry lease-in** (T.B.104(4)).
- Pre-flight inspection **before each flight** (T.A.201(1)(h)).
- Level 1 finding: corrective action **before further flight** + notify State of Registry (T.B.202(4)).
- Suspension/revocation of CAMO certificate invalidates the AOC (CAME statement).

## 3. Records and Documents

**Aircraft records required (T.A.201(1)(j))**:
1. Total time in service (hours, cycles, calendar time as appropriate) of aircraft and all life-limited components.
2. Current status of compliance with T.A.201(1)(f) (State of Registry ADs + EASA MSI/ADs).
3. Current status of compliance with the maintenance programme.
4. Current status of modifications and repairs with details and substantiating data showing State of Registry compliance.
- GM: records must let CAMO and CA establish the airworthy condition throughout the lease period.

**Release to service**: issued by qualified organisation per State of Registry, signed, containing basic details of maintenance.

**CA per-aircraft records (T.B.104(2))**: copy of CofA; relevant correspondence; reports of inspections and surveys; exemptions and enforcement actions.

**EASA Form 13T — Part-CAMO and T.A. Subpart G Approval Recommendation Report** (Appendix II to AMC T.B.702, ED 2021/009/R):
- Part 1 General: organisation, approval ref, requested rating / EASA Form 14 or AOC date, other approvals, facility addresses, audit period, dates, references, persons interviewed, surveyor, office, signatures, completion date.
- Part 2 Compliance audit review (5 columns, tick/cross/N/A/N/R): T.A.201; CAMO.A.115, .120, .125 + T.A.711, .130, .135 + T.A.715, .140, .150 + T.A.716, .155, .160, .200 + T.A.712, .202, .205, .215, .220 + T.A.714, .300 + T.A.704, .305 + T.A.706, .310, .315 + T.A.708, .320, .325 + T.A.709.
- Part 3 CAME compliance: Part 0 (0.1-0.7 incl. AltMoC procedure), Part 1 (1.1a records/ATL, 1.1b MEL, 1.2 AMP, 1.3 records, 1.4 ADs, 1.5 AMP effectiveness, 1.6 non-mandatory mods, 1.7 repairs/mods, 1.8 defect reports, 1.9 engineering, 1.10 reliability, 1.11 pre-flight, 1.12 weighing, 1.13 maintenance check flights), Part 2 management system (2.1-2.11 incl. compliance monitoring 2.8.1-2.8.6), Part 3 contracted maintenance (3.1, 3.2 product audit), Part 4 airworthiness review (4.1-4.8 incl. ARC issue and extension, import recommendations), Part 4B permit to fly (4B.1-4B.5), Part 5 supporting documents (5.1-5.7), Part 6 Part-T procedures (6.1.1-6.1.10, 6.2.1-6.2.2).
- Part 4 Findings: ref, audit ref, finding, level, corrective action, date due, date closed, reference.
- Part 5 Recommendation: terms of approval recommended or continuation of EASA Form 14 terms; recommending inspector; date; review.

**CAME additions for Part-T (Appendix I to AMC T.A.704)**:
- 0.1 AM statement referencing compliance with Part-CAMO, Part-M and Part-T; CA may limit/suspend/revoke; suspension/revocation of CAMO certificate invalidates the AOC.
- 0.2 Scope of work table: aircraft type/series; date included; AMP or generic/baseline AMP; registration(s); owner/operator; CAMO contract reference; Part-T flag; State of Registry. Updated each time aircraft added/removed, or each time a type/significant number changes with pointer to current list.
- New Part 6:
  - 6.1.1 (a) records system and technical log; (b) MEL responsibilities.
  - 6.1.2 AMP: State of Registry AMP requirements; development/update/approval or acceptance; sources and mandatory tasks identified.
  - 6.1.3 (a) access to and processing of flight hours/cycles; (b) records table: document family, name, retention period, responsible person, place of retention; (c) preservation (fire, flood, non-alteration esp. computer records); (d) transfer-in of records before leasing (status of compliance, releases, mod/repair approval and substantiation, MSI compliance) and transfer-out.
  - 6.1.4 MSI from State of Registry and EASA: (a) acquisition sources (State of Registry, manufacturer, TCH, EASA); (b) decision/analysis, conflict resolution between State of Registry MSI and EASA MSI/EU requirements, info to maintenance orgs, emergency MSI procedure; (c) control: closed-loop per new/revised MSI per aircraft: not applicable / applicable and not yet performed but not overdue / performed with repetitive inspections identified and performed; continuous or scheduled review.
  - 6.1.5 Mods and repairs: State of Registry requirements, design data approval, classification, CAMO approval before embodiment.
  - 6.1.6 Defect reports: analysis (feeds AMP evolution and non-mandatory mod policy); liaison with TCH and TC authority for fleet-relevant defects; deferred defect policy per State of Registry (structural defects/cracks not covered by MEL/CDL; liaison with manufacturer and State of Registry).
  - 6.1.7 Reliability programme (scope, organisation, data, analysis, corrective action/AMP amendment, reliability meetings with CA; airframe/propulsion/component).
  - 6.1.8 Pre-flight inspection consistency with maintenance scope; plus aircraft preparation, subcontracted ground handling, cargo/baggage security, refuelling control, snow/ice/de-icing residue/dust/sand contamination.
  - 6.1.9 Aircraft weighing (EU operational + State of Registry requirements; after major mod; who weighs, procedure, W&B calc).
  - 6.1.10 Check flight criteria and release procedures (after heavy check, engine/flight control removal/installation).
  - 6.2.1 Contracted maintenance: contract development per Appendix IV to AMC1 CAMO.A.315(c); work order template (in Part 5.1); contractor selection verifying Subpart E compliance and industrial capacity; contract review.
  - 6.2.2 Aircraft audit before lease (inspection of aircraft and records: airworthy, State of Registry + Part-T + EU requirements, emergency/operational equipment per EU ops and airspace rules, maintenance/MSI done, mods/repairs compliant and recorded) and during lease (procedures, contract compliance, continued Part-T compliance).

## 4. Defined Terms

- **Part-T aircraft**: aircraft registered in a third country, safety oversight not delegated to a Member State, dry leased-in by an EU-licensed air carrier (Art. 1(b)).
- **State of Registry**: the third country; its requirements govern AMP, defect rectification standard, mods/repairs, release to service, maintenance organisation approval, maintenance data.
- **MSI** (mandatory safety information): from State of Registry and EASA, including ADs.
- **Level 1 / Level 2 finding** (T.B.202 definitions above).
- **ICA**: instructions for continued airworthiness (part of applicable maintenance data, AMC T.A.709).

## 5. Software Implications (Airworthiness+)

- Aircraft entity needs: registration state (third country), "Part-T" flag, lease-in start/end dates, lessee AOC/operator, CA (AOC-issuing State), CAMO, State of Registry; whether oversight delegated (then Part-M M.A.201 rather than Part-T).
- **Dual AD/MSI tracking**: applicability and compliance for both State of Registry ADs and EASA ADs/MSI per aircraft, with conflict-resolution notes; closed-loop status per MSI per aircraft (N/A / open-not-overdue / complied + repetitive tracking); emergency MSI handling.
- Records: hours/cycles/calendar for aircraft and every LLP; AMP compliance status; mod/repair status with State-of-Registry approval and substantiation data; retention >= 24 months or until superseded; CAMO archival; CA wants records available on request; CA keeps 4 years after lease end.
- AMP: per State of Registry and ICAO Annex 6; maintenance data acceptable to State of Registry, in acceptable language; ICA library.
- Maintenance organisation register: State of Registry approval reference, scope, occurrence reporting, manual; Subpart E verification evidence (ICAO Annex 6 Part I 8.7 approval as input).
- Contract management: contract per lease (<= 7 months typical), work orders for unscheduled line/component work; lease-end alert.
- Pre-lease and in-lease aircraft audit checklists (Appendix I 6.2.2) and records transfer-in/out workflows.
- CAME scope-of-work table generation including Part-T column and State of Registry.
- Release to service records must capture basic details of maintenance and be signed.
- Finding tracker with root cause/contributing factors fields (T.A.716) and "corrective action before further flight" grounding flag for level 1.
- UK: if UK lacks Part-T, gate the feature behind jurisdiction; UK operators wet/dry-leasing foreign-registered aircraft may be under different UK CAA rules (guess).

## 6. Cross-References

- Art. 1(a)(ii), Art. 1(b), Art. 3(6) of 1321/2014; Reg. (EC) 1008/2008 (air carrier licensing); Reg. (EU) 2018/1139 Annex V essential requirements.
- Air Ops: ORO.AOC.110 (lease conditions), ARO.OPS.110(a)(1) (CA approval of dry lease-in).
- Part-M: M.A.201 (delegated-oversight aircraft), AMC M.A.301(a) (pre-flight inspection content), M.B.102(c)/(d) AMC (CA staff and procedures), M.B.104(a),(b),(c),(f) (record-keeping), M.B.105 (information exchange).
- Part-CAMO: CAMO.A.115, .120, .125(d)(3) (subcontracting limited CAW tasks), .130 (changes), .135, .140, .150, .155, .160, .200, .202, .205, .215, .220(a), .300 (incl. (a)(12), (a)(13)), .305 (incl. (a)(3)-(5), (b)(2), (g) competence assessment), .310, .315 (Appendix IV to AMC1 CAMO.A.315(c) contracted maintenance), .320, .325; CAMO.B.305, .310, .350. EASA Form 14 (CAMO certificate).
- ICAO Annex 6 (AMP, Part I Section 8.7 maintenance organisation approval), ICAO Annex 8 (CofA).

## 7. Notable AMC and GM

- GM T.1: applicability boundary (delegated oversight -> Part-M; not delegated -> Part-T).
- AMC T.A.201(1)(h): pre-flight content per AMC M.A.301(a).
- AMC1 T.A.201(3): CAMO responsible for airworthy condition; must be satisfied before intended flight that required maintenance done; process to verify Subpart E compliance of maintenance organisation.
- AMC2 T.A.201(3): contract specifies responsibilities and work clearly; CAMO should consider checking contracted work at the facilities.
- AMC3 T.A.201(3): contract for lease duration (<= 7 months); work orders for unscheduled line/component maintenance up to engines.
- GM1 T.A.501: State of Registry approval under ICAO Annex 6 Part I 8.7 as an input. AMC1 T.A.501(3): occurrence reporting procedure transmits faults/malfunctions/defects to operator, type design organisation, State of Registry.
- AMC T.A.706: knowledge by training/experience; CAMO.A.305(g) competence assessment to cover Part-T.
- GM T.A.708: existing Part-CAMO procedures may be adapted or new ones developed.
- AMC T.A.709: maintenance data = ICA + State of Registry requirements/procedures/standards/MSI + EASA requirements/MSI; language acceptable to CA.
- AMC T.A.711: CAMO may subcontract limited Part-T CAW tasks under CAMO.A.125(d)(3) to an organisation under its quality system and listed on the approval certificate.
- AMC T.B.102(3)/(4): CA staff need third-country requirement knowledge; procedures for coordination with State of Registry.
- AMC T.B.702: Form 13T for audits; if CAMO not approved for the type, apply for CAMO.A.130 change concurrently; if already approved, Part-T approval is a prior-approval change via CAME amendment approval.

**What this chunk covers:** ML.1, ML.A.101, ML.A.201, ML.A.202, ML.A.301 to ML.A.305 and ML.A.307, with their AMC and GM. The chunk ends at ML.A.307. There is no ML.A.306 in the text. Part-ML has no "technical log" point, unlike M.A.306 in Part-M; the aircraft logbook under ML.A.305 does that job.

Where this chunk mentions those points, the notes below record the reference only.

**UK caveat (applies throughout):** UK retained Part-ML (UK Reg 1321/2014 as retained, administered by the CAA) is broadly the same text. These are guesses that need checking against CAA sources:
- "Agency" becomes the CAA. "Member State of registry" becomes the UK.
- "EASA Form 1" becomes "CAA Form 1". "EASA Form AMP" may be a CAA equivalent (CAA uses forms such as SRG 1724 / "Part-ML AMP template"; unverified).
- Part 21 Light (Annex Ib, "declaration of design compliance", 21L points) is an EU 2022 addition. The UK probably has not adopted it, so references to the "declarant" are likely absent in the UK.
- Regulation 2023/989 amendments to ML.A.302 (pilot-owner wording in (e)(4)) may not be in UK retained law or may differ.
- The UK also has national schemes: LAA/BMAA permit aircraft are outside Part-ML; the CAA ANO Part 3 governs non-Part-21 aircraft.
- The UK also had "UK Part-ML extension of light aircraft scope". Unverified.

## 1. Scope, point by point

| Point | Status | One-line summary |
|---|---|---|
| ML.1(a) | IR | Part-ML applies to non-complex motor-powered aircraft that are not listed on the AOC of an air carrier licensed under Reg 1008/2008, if they are one of: (1) aeroplanes with MTOM of 2 730 kg or less; (2) rotorcraft with MTOM of 1 200 kg or less, certified for up to 4 occupants; (3) other ELA2 aircraft. |
| ML.1(b) | IR | The competent authority is the authority designated by the Member State of registry. |
| ML.1(c) | IR | Definitions: independent certifying staff, maintenance organisation, owner (see section 4). |
| ML.A.101 | IR | Section A sets out the measures that keep the aircraft airworthy and the conditions for persons and organisations involved. |
| ML.A.201(a) | IR | The owner is responsible for continuing airworthiness. There is no flight unless four conditions are met: the aircraft is airworthy; operational and emergency equipment is correctly installed and serviceable, or clearly identified as unserviceable; the airworthiness certificate is valid; maintenance follows the AMP of ML.A.302. |
| ML.A.201(b) | IR | For a leased aircraft, the responsibilities of (a) pass to the lessee if the lessee is identified in the registration document or the lease. |
| ML.A.201(c) | IR | Anyone performing maintenance is responsible for the tasks they perform. |
| ML.A.201(d) | IR | The PIC is responsible for the pre-flight inspection. It is done by the pilot or another qualified person; no maintenance organisation or certifying staff is needed. |
| ML.A.201(e) | IR | Commercial ATO/DTO, non-Part-NCO, Part-BOP Subpart-ADD and Part-SAO Subpart-DEC operators must: be a CAMO/CAO or contract one using the Appendix I contract; have all maintenance done by approved maintenance organisations; and satisfy (a). |
| ML.A.201(f) | IR | Other owners **may** contract a CAMO or CAO in writing per Appendix I. The organisation then takes on responsibility for those tasks. Without a contract, the owner is responsible. |
| ML.A.201(g) | IR | The owner must give the competent authority access to the aircraft and its records. |
| ML.A.201(h) | IR | An AOC aircraft used for non-commercial or specialised operations (ORO.GEN.310 / NCO.GEN.104) must have its continuing airworthiness tasks done by the AOC holder's CAMO or CAO. |
| ML.A.202(a)-(b) | IR | Persons or organisations responsible under ML.A.201 report any condition that endangers flight safety to (1) the competent authority of the state of registry, and of the state of the operator if different, and (2) the TC/STC holder. Reports are made in the way the authority determines and contain all pertinent known information. |
| ML.A.202(c) | IR | Under a contracted maintenance or ARC arrangement, the contractor also reports to the owner and, if different, to the CAMO/CAO. |
| ML.A.202(d) | IR | Reports are due "as soon as possible, but no later than 72 hours" from identifying the condition, unless exceptional circumstances apply. |
| ML.A.301 | IR | Continuing airworthiness tasks: (a) pre-flight inspections; (b) rectifying defects and damage using ML.A.304/ML.A.401 data, taking the MEL and CDL into account where they exist; (c) all maintenance per the AMP; (d) applicable ADs, operational directives with a continuing airworthiness impact, Agency continuing airworthiness requirements, and immediate safety measures from the competent authority; (e) modifications and repairs per ML.A.304; (f) maintenance check flights when necessary. |
| ML.A.302(a) | IR | Each aircraft's maintenance is organised under an AMP. |
| ML.A.302(b) | IR | The AMP and its amendments are either declared by the owner (no CAMO/CAO) or approved by the CAMO/CAO managing the aircraft. The declarer or approver keeps it up to date. |
| ML.A.302(c)(1)-(9) | IR | AMP content: identification; basis (MIP, DAH ICA or declarant ICA); additional or alternative actions; mandatory information; customisation factors; whether the pilot-owner is authorised; owner statement; CAMO/CAO signature with deviation justifications; annual review. |
| ML.A.302(d) | IR | MIP intervals and tolerances, and the mandatory MIP content by aircraft category. There is no MIP for rotorcraft or airships; their AMP is based on the DAH ICA. |
| ML.A.302(e) | IR | Derogation: no declaration, no approval and no AMP document are needed if four conditions are met (see section 2). |
| ML.A.302(f) | IR | Under that derogation, the AMP consists of: the DAH ICA; non-mandatory recommendations such as TBO; mandatory continuing airworthiness information; and operational or airspace equipment tasks. |
| ML.A.303 | IR | Applicable ADs are carried out within the requirements of the AD unless the Agency specifies otherwise. |
| ML.A.304 | IR | Repairers assess damage. Modifications and repairs use approved or declared data: Agency; Part 21 DOA; 21.A.90B / 21.A.431B (CS-STAN); 21L.A.62 / 102 / 202 / 222; or a Part 21 Light declarant. |
| ML.A.305 | IR | Continuing airworthiness record system: CRS entry deadline, logbooks, status content, component entries, control, corrections and retention periods. |
| ML.A.307 | IR | Records transfer on change of owner or on contracting a CAMO/CAO. Retention periods carry over to the new holder. |

**Status of the AMC and GM in the chunk:**
- GM: GM1 ML.A.201; GM1 ML.A.201(e); GM1 ML.A.201(f); GM1 ML.A.201(h); GM1 ML.A.301(f); GM1 ML.A.302; GM2 ML.A.302; GM1 ML.A.302(c)(2)(b); GM1 ML.A.302(c)(3); GM1 ML.A.302(c)(4); GM1 ML.A.302(d)(2); GM1 ML.A.302(d)(2)(d).
- AMC: AMC1 ML.A.202; AMC1 ML.A.302; AMC2 ML.A.302 (EASA Form AMP); AMC1 ML.A.302(c); AMC1 ML.A.302(c)(9); AMC1 ML.A.302(d) (the three MIPs); AMC1 ML.A.305.
