## 7. Notable AMC and GM (detail)
- **AMC1 ML.A.402**: acceptable maintenance records are the ticked and signed 100-h/annual checklist plus a CRS listing the tasks. This supports a checklist-based e-record with signatures.
- **AMC1 ML.A.402(b)(7)**: sign-off only after task completion. Grouping must keep critical steps identifiable. Supervised staff work is countersigned. Software: per-step sign-off, critical-step markers, countersignature.
- **AMC1/AMC2 ML.A.402(b)(8)**: the four categories of critical tasks and the two error-capture methods (re-inspection by the same person when alone, or independent inspection). Software: a critical-task flag requires an error-capture record before the CRS.
- **AMC1 ML.A.403**: defects are malfunctions seen in flight, or faults found by inspection or test. Pilot comments are not automatically defects. Keep a separate "observation" record type.
- **GM1 ML.A.403**: consult available certifying staff before deferring. A pilot under NCO (or a non-ADD balloon or non-DEC sailplane) can defer required equipment whether or not a CAMO/CAO is contracted, but needs owner or CAMO/CAO agreement. Defines "required".
- **AMC1 ML.A.403(d)**: deferred defects are communicated before crew arrival, listed on the deferred list, fixed at the next appropriate event, and keep the original date if re-entered.
- **GM1 ML.A.501(a)**: new components under 21.A.307(b) / 21L.A.193(b) need no Form 1. Their accompanying document conditions are in point (c).
- **AMC1 ML.A.501(a)(ii)**: the 9-item list of Form 1 equivalents with date cut-offs (see 2.4). Implement as a picklist with date validation.
- **AMC1 ML.A.501(e)**: balloon basket, burner and cylinder swaps need no Form 1 if serviceable records are accessible. Watch inspection dates. Maintenance on them still needs a Form 1, an equivalent, or a balloon logbook release.
- **GM1 ML.A.502**: independent certifying staff may release component maintenance only where ML.A.201 lets them maintain and they are competent (not for ADD balloons).
- **GM1 ML.A.502(c)**: the declaration of maintenance accomplished is free form and needs no approval. Records must show the component was first installed new as a (b)(3)–(6) component. Reject unreadable or unsatisfactory declarations.
- **AMC1 ML.A.801 (SC/SR)**: the long guidance in 2.5. Key points: the installer is responsible for CS-STAN compliance; Form 123; the same signer for Form 123 and the CRS; a logbook reference; owner copies; one Form 123 for related SCs; the owner, CAMO or CAO assesses ICA impact on the AMP; information is consulted at the airworthiness review.
- **AMC1 ML.A.801(e)**: the two statement wordings; task reference with revision; life-limit relative timing; work-pack summarising; e-signature (personal card plus PIN, authority satisfied, stamp optional); legible records; independent certifying staff keep proof records.
- **AMC1 ML.A.801(f)**: release incomplete maintenance before a required flight, with the operator responsible for the maintenance check flight, then a full CRS after.
- **AMC1 ML.A.803**: own-work-only rule; joint-owner list in the AMP; equivalent licence; medical not needed.
- **GM1 ML.A.901**: freedom to choose the reviewer. No obligation on listed parties to accept.
- **AMC1 ML.A.903(h)**: the AMP review at the airworthiness review is by the reviewer, not responsible for AMP completeness, sampling allowed.
- **GM1 ML.A.904(c);(d)**: "corresponding aircraft" means meeting certifying-staff requirements at the time of the review. The authorisation needs a knowledge assessment plus a supervised review.
- **AMC1 ML.B.201**: the AMP data-collection template (see 3.10).
- **AMC1 ML.B.303**: reuse the Part-M survey programme structure.
- **AMC1 to Appendix II**: the task lists are representative, not exhaustive. Periodic inspections are eligible only task by task. A 50-h/6-month aeroplane inspection and a 1-year glider inspection may normally qualify. `**` means no IFR until released by certifying staff.

### Possible UK differences (guesses, verify)
- Form names: "CAA Form 15c" / "UK CAA Form 1".
- The ARC copy goes to the UK CAA within 10 days.
- References to "Member State" or "Agency" become the CAA.
- ARC mutual-recognition and EU transfer provisions do not apply. Aircraft from the EU register are treated as imports.
- Pilot-owner tasks in the UK may also be shaped by CAA guidance (for example CAP 1789 or similar UK Part-ML guidance).
- Part 21 Light (Reg. 2022/1360) and ED Decision 2023/013/R changes (Form 123 Issue 2, declared-design references, the equivalence item for a declaration of maintenance accomplished) may not be adopted, or may be adopted on a different timeline, in UK law.
- UK-registered aircraft outside the Part-ML scope (Annex I aircraft, LAA/BMAA permits) follow national rules instead.


# Chunk 19: Part-CAMO General and Section A

# Chunk 19: Part-CAMO (Annex Vc) – General and Section A (Organisation Requirements)

Source: EASA Easy Access Rules for Continuing Airworthiness (Reg. (EU) No 1321/2014), Annex Vc. Chunk file: `/home/claude/r1321/chunks/19.txt` (1,287 lines, read in full).
Part-CAMO has no Subparts. The chunk covers GM1 to Annex Vc (definitions), CAMO.A.005 to CAMO.A.325, and their AMC/GM. Section B (authority requirements, CAMO.B.xxx) and the Appendices are **not** in this chunk. Referenced but not reproduced here: Appendix I (CAMO certificate, EASA Form 14), Appendix I to AMC1 CAMO.A.115 (EASA Form 2), Appendix II to AMC1 CAMO.A.125(d)(3) (subcontracting), Appendix III to AMC4 CAMO.A.305(g) (fuel tank safety training), Appendix IV to AMC1 CAMO.A.315(c) (maintenance contracts).

Amending acts cited in the source: IR from Reg. (EU) 2019/1383 (the main Part-CAMO text), 2020/270, 2022/410 (single air carrier business grouping, M.A.201(ea)), 2022/1360 (Part 21 Light in occurrence reporting), 2023/203 (Part-IS). AMC/GM from ED Decisions 2020/002/R, 2021/009/R, 2022/011/R, 2022/017/R, 2023/013/R.

**UK note (guesswork, verify against UK CAA text):** UK retained Part-CAMO (from Reg. 2019/1383) is close to this text. Items likely absent or different in the UK version are flagged "UK?" below. The most likely differences are: everything from Reg. 2022/410 (single air carrier business grouping / M.A.201(ea), ML AMP approval privilege wording), 2022/1360 (Part 21 Light), 2023/203 (CAMO.A.200A Part-IS), and AMC/GM from ED Decisions 2022/011, 2022/017 and 2023/013. Also "competent authority" is the UK CAA; "Agency" is replaced by the CAA; EASA Forms become CAA Forms (CAA Form 2, CAA Form 14); "Member State" becomes the UK; Reg. 376/2014 and 2015/1018 are the UK-retained versions (MOR reporting to the CAA).

## 1. Scope (point by point)

| Point | Title | One-line summary |
|---|---|---|
| GM1 to Annex Vc | Definitions | Definitions used in Part-CAMO AMC/GM (audit, competency, correction, corrective action, hazard, near-miss, post holder, working days, etc.). See Section 4. |
| CAMO.A.005 | Scope | Requirements for an organisation to get or keep a certificate to manage continuing airworthiness of aircraft and components for installation. |
| CAMO.A.105 | Competent authority | Which authority oversees the CAMO: the State of principal place of business (if not part of an AOC, or if contracted under M.A.201(ea)); the State of the operator (if the approval is in an AOC); a reallocated State or EASA (Art. 64/65 of 2018/1139); EASA if the principal place of business is outside the Member States. |
| CAMO.A.115 | Application for an organisation certificate | Apply in the form set by the authority. Initial applicants must submit pre-audit results and compliance documentation, including the procedure for changes not needing prior approval. |
| CAMO.A.120 | Means of compliance | Alternative means of compliance (AltMoC) may be used only after a full description and compliance assessment are submitted and prior approval is given (notification under CAMO.B.120). |
| CAMO.A.125 | Terms of approval and privileges | The certificate (Appendix I), or the AOC for licensed air carriers, sets the approval. Base privileges (d): manage CAW; subcontract limited tasks; extend ARCs; approve ML AMPs. Optional privileges: (e) airworthiness reviews and ARC issue or recommendation; (f) permit to fly issue. |
| CAMO.A.130 | Changes to the organisation | Lists the changes needing prior approval (scope or terms, nominated persons, their reporting lines, the change procedure itself). All other changes go through the agreed change procedure. |
| CAMO.A.135 | Continued validity | The certificate stays valid while the organisation complies, gives the authority access, and the certificate is not surrendered or revoked. Rules for AOC linkage. Return the certificate on revocation or surrender. |
| CAMO.A.140 | Access | Give authorised persons access at any time to facilities, aircraft, documents, records, data and procedures, including those of contracted and subcontracted parties. |
| CAMO.A.150 | Findings | After a finding is notified: identify root causes and contributing factors, define a corrective action plan (CAP), and show it has been implemented, all within the period agreed under CAMO.B.350. |
| CAMO.A.155 | Immediate reaction to a safety problem | Implement safety measures mandated by the authority (CAMO.B.135) and relevant EASA mandatory safety information. |
| CAMO.A.160 | Occurrence reporting | Run an occurrence reporting system meeting 376/2014 and 2015/1018. Report to the authority and the design organisation within 72 hours. Send follow-up reports. |
| CAMO.A.200 | Management system | SMS-style management system: accountabilities, safety policy, hazard and risk management, training and competence, documentation, compliance monitoring with feedback to the accountable manager. Scaled to size. May be integrated with other approvals. Must be integrated with the operator's system for licensed air carriers. Must be harmonised within a business grouping. |
| CAMO.A.200A | Information security management system | ISMS per Reg. (EU) 2023/203 (Part-IS), applicable from 22 February 2026. UK? (probably not adopted in the UK) |
| CAMO.A.202 | Internal safety reporting scheme | Internal scheme to collect and evaluate occurrences, errors, near misses and hazards. Identify causes. Give subcontractors access. Cooperate on investigations. |
| CAMO.A.205 | Contracting and subcontracting | Contracted maintenance and subcontracted CAW tasks must conform to the requirements and be covered by hazard management. Subcontractors work under the CAMO's approval. The authority must have access to them. |
| CAMO.A.215 | Facilities | Suitable office accommodation at appropriate locations for the CAMO.A.305 personnel. |
| CAMO.A.220 | Record-keeping | CAW records, ARC, recommendation and PtF copies (3 years after the aircraft is permanently transferred), management system records and contracts (5 years), personnel records (employment plus 3 years). Storage must be protected. |
| CAMO.A.300 | Continuing airworthiness management exposition (CAME) | Mandatory CAME contents (14 items). The initial issue is approved by the authority. Amendments follow the CAME procedures. |
| CAMO.A.305 | Personnel requirements | Accountable manager and their duties. Nominated persons for CAW management, compliance monitoring and safety management. Air carrier post holder. Staff planning. Airworthiness review staff (ARS). ARC extension staff. Competency control. |
| CAMO.A.310 | Airworthiness review staff qualifications | 5 years' CAW experience, a Part-66 licence or aeronautical degree (or 5 more years' experience), formal maintenance training, an appropriate position, authority acceptance after a supervised review, and recent experience. |
| CAMO.A.315 | Continuing airworthiness management | Manage CAW per Part-M or Part-ML Subpart C. Per aircraft: AMP, copy of the AMP to the owner, mod and repair data, non-mandatory mods (CMPA or air carrier), use of approved maintenance organisations, ordering and supervising maintenance. Maintenance contracts or work orders. Human factors. |
| CAMO.A.320 | Airworthiness review | Airworthiness reviews are performed per M.A.901 or ML.A.903. |
| CAMO.A.325 | Continuing airworthiness management data | Hold and use current maintenance data (M.A.401 / ML.A.401). Data may be supplied by the customer under contract and kept only for the contract's duration unless it is a record under CAMO.A.220(a). |

## 2. Obligations (with exact numbers)

### 2.1 Certification, application and AltMoC
- **Application (CAMO.A.115):** use the authority's form and manner. AMC1: **EASA Form 2** (Appendix I to AMC1 CAMO.A.115) or equivalent. One Form 2 can cover several certificate types under 1321/2014.
- **Initial application contents (CAMO.A.115(b)):** (1) results of an internal **pre-audit** against Part-M, Part-ML and Part-CAMO; (2) compliance documentation, including the **procedure for changes not requiring prior approval**.
- **AMC1 CAMO.A.115(b)(2):** the minimum documentation is the CAME, including:
  - for CAT, commercial specialised operations and commercial ATO/DTO operations, a description of the aircraft technical log (ATL) system;
  - the technical content of any subcontract for CAW management tasks.
  On request, the CAMO must show arrangements exist for all base and scheduled line maintenance "for an appropriate period of time". If M.A.201(ea) applies, the CAW management contract with the operator(s) (Appendix I to Part-M) is submitted with the CAME. UK?
- **AMC2 CAMO.A.115:** submit drafts early. Certification cannot happen until the completed documents are received. The pre-audit shows internal verification of compliance and lets the authority size its oversight.
- **GM1 CAMO.A.115(b):** for an initial certificate the authority may limit the scope of changes not requiring prior approval for the first period of operation.
- **AltMoC (CAMO.A.120):** before use, give the authority a full description, the relevant manual or procedure revisions, and a compliance assessment. Use only after **prior approval** and notification under CAMO.B.120. Changes to an AltMoC need prior approval (GM1 CAMO.A.130(b)). The CAME lists currently approved AltMoCs (CAMO.A.300(a)(14)).

### 2.2 Privileges (CAMO.A.125)
- (a) The approval is shown on the certificate (Appendix I).
- (b) For air carriers licensed under Reg. 1008/2008, the approval is part of the AOC, except when the CAMO is contracted under M.A.201(ea) by operators forming a single air carrier business grouping.
- (c) The scope of work is specified in the CAME.
- (d) Base privileges:
  1. manage CAW of aircraft listed on the certificate (not licensed air carrier aircraft);
  2. manage CAW of licensed air carrier aircraft listed on both the certificate and the AOC, or when M.A.201(ea) applies;
  3. arrange for limited CAW tasks to be done by subcontracted organisations working under its management system, as listed on the certificate;
  4. **extend an ARC** under M.A.901(f) or ML.A.901(c);
  5. **approve the AMP** under ML.A.302(b)(2) for Part-ML aircraft.
- (e) Optional, only for organisations with their principal place of business in a Member State: **airworthiness reviews** per M.A.901 or ML.A.903, and
  1. issue the ARC and extend it under M.A.901(c)(2) and (e)(2) or ML.A.901(c);
  2. issue a **recommendation** for the airworthiness review to the State of registry authority (M.A.901(d) or M.A.904(b)).
- (f) Optional, only with (e): issue a **permit to fly** per 21.A.711(d) for the particular aircraft for which it may issue ARCs, when attesting conformity with approved flight conditions. Needs an adequate CAME procedure.
  - GM1 CAMO.A.125(f): for Part-M aircraft used by licensed air carriers and aircraft above **2 730 kg MTOM**, a PtF only for aircraft in a controlled environment managed by that CAMO. For Part-M aircraft of 2 730 kg MTOM or less not used by licensed air carriers, and for all Part-ML aircraft, a PtF can be issued for any aircraft.
- GM1 CAMO.A.125(e):
  - A CAMO may hold (d) only and contract airworthiness reviews to another suitably approved CAMO for the same type, which need not be linked to an AOC holder.
  - (e) for a type requires (d) for that type.
  - The CAMO need not currently manage that type to do ARs on it. Not managing a type does not by itself lead to the type being removed, provided all Part-CAMO requirements (facilities, documentation, personnel, management system) remain met.

### 2.3 Subcontracting of CAW management tasks (AMC1 CAMO.A.125(d)(3), CAMO.A.205, GM1 CAMO.A.205)
- The subcontractor works as an integral part of the CAMO's management system, regardless of its own approvals (CAMO or Part-145). The CAMO remains **accountable** for the tasks.
- Control is exercised by active control (direct involvement) and/or by endorsing the subcontractor's recommendations.
- **Permitted subcontracted tasks (limit):**
  1. AD analysis and planning;
  2. SB analysis;
  3. planning of maintenance;
  4. reliability monitoring and engine health monitoring;
  5. AMP development and amendments;
  6. other activities agreed by the authority that do not limit the CAMO's responsibilities.
- Controls are reflected in the contract and in line with the CAME. The management system is considered extended to the subcontractor.
- Normally **one subcontractor per aircraft type** for any combination of Appendix II activities, except for engines and APUs. With more than one, the CAMO must show coordination controls and clear responsibilities.
- **No further sub-subcontracting** may be authorised.
- Contracts must be acceptable to the authority. Subcontract **only to organisations specified by the authority on EASA Form 14** (the certificate). Adding a subcontractor is a change needing prior approval (GM1 CAMO.A.130(a)(1)).
- The subcontractor notifies the CAMO of changes affecting the contract as soon as practical, and the CAMO informs the authority. Failure to do so may invalidate the authority's acceptance of the contract.
- CAMO.A.205(a): when contracting maintenance or subcontracting any part of CAW management, the activities must conform to the requirements, and the related hazards must be covered by the management system. (b) The subcontractor works under the CAMO's approval, and the authority gets access to it.
- GM1 CAMO.A.205:
  - All subcontracted activities are subject to hazard identification and risk management (CAMO.A.200(a)(3)) and compliance monitoring (CAMO.A.200(a)(6)), whatever the subcontractor's approval status.
  - Compliance monitoring must at least check that each contracted maintenance organisation's approval **covers the contracted activities and is still valid**.
  - Establish occurrence reporting interfaces with contracted MOs (their own reporting duty is not replaced) and internal safety reporting interfaces with subcontractors.

### 2.4 Changes to the organisation (CAMO.A.130 + AMC/GM)
- **Prior approval required (a):**
  1. changes affecting the scope of the certificate or the terms of approval;
  2. changes to nominated persons under CAMO.A.305(a)(3) to (a)(5) and (b)(2);
  3. changes to reporting lines between those persons and the accountable manager;
  4. the procedure for changes not requiring prior approval.
- **(b)** Apply **before** the change and provide the relevant documentation. Implement only after **formal approval** (CAMO.B.330). Operate under any conditions the authority sets during the change.
- **(c)** Changes not needing prior approval are managed and notified per the agreed procedure (CAMO.A.115(b), approved under CAMO.B.310(h)).
- **AMC1 time frames:**
  - Application for amendment of the certificate at least **30 working days** before the intended change.
  - Planned change of a nominated person: inform the authority at least **20 working days** before.
  - Unforeseen changes: notify at the earliest opportunity.
- **AMC2:** manage the safety risk of changes via management of change (AMC1 CAMO.A.200(a)(3)(e)). For prior-approval changes, do a **risk assessment** and provide it to the authority on request.
- **GM1 CAMO.A.130(a)(1) examples of scope or terms changes:**
  1. name of the organisation;
  2. principal place of business;
  3. additional aircraft type, series or group;
  4. accountable manager;
  5. additional subcontracted organisation;
  6. M.A.201(ea) contracts with business grouping operators.
- **GM2:** a change of name requires a **new application as a matter of urgency**. If it is the only change, the previous documentation can be resubmitted.
- **GM1 CAMO.A.130(b): other changes needing prior approval:**
  - (a) AltMoC (CAMO.A.120(b));
  - (b) the CAME procedure for an airworthiness review under supervision of the organisation's authorised ARS (CAMO.A.310(c));
  - (c) the competency procedure (CAMO.A.305(g));
  - (d) the system for reporting safety performance and compliance to the authority when the oversight planning cycle is extended beyond **36 months** (CAMO.B.305(d));
  - (e) the indirect AMP approval procedure for Part-M aircraft (M.A.302(c)).
- GM1 CAMO.A.130 explains the structure: (a) lists specific prior-approval cases; (b) covers every case where the Regulation requires approval; (c) allows agreed changes without prior approval, depending on compliance and safety performance and the organisation's change management capability.

### 2.5 Continued validity and access (CAMO.A.135, CAMO.A.140)
- The certificate is valid while: the organisation complies (taking into account findings handling under CAMO.B.350); the authority is granted access; and it is not surrendered or revoked. There is **no expiry date**: validity is unlimited, subject to these conditions.
- For licensed air carriers, termination, suspension or revocation of the AOC automatically invalidates the CAMO certificate for the AOC registrations, unless the authority states otherwise.
- Exception for M.A.201(ea): the CAMO certificate is not invalidated, but the Appendix I (Part-M) contract becomes void. UK?
- Return the certificate **without delay** on revocation or surrender.
- **Access** "at any time" to any facility, aircraft, document, record, data, procedure or other material, whether contracted or subcontracted or not, for persons authorised by the competent authority, or by the authority acting under CAMO.B.300(d) or (e).

### 2.6 Findings (CAMO.A.150 + AMC/GM)
- After a finding is notified (CAMO.B.350):
  1. identify root cause(s) and contributing factors;
  2. define a **corrective action plan**;
  3. demonstrate implementation to the authority's satisfaction.
- All three must be done **within the period agreed** with the authority (CAMO.B.350). Level 1 and 2 definitions and time limits are in Section B, not in this chunk.
- AMC1: the action plan addresses the effects, root cause(s) and contributing factor(s), and as needed **correction/containment, corrective action and preventive action**.
- AMC2: if a finding (authority or internal) affects management system harmonisation under M.A.201(ea), inform the operator(s) through an agreed channel. If the group uses common standards, inform the group management board. UK?
- GM1 causal analysis: focus on **why**, not who. Consider systemic factors (regulatory, HF, organisational, technical). Avoid simple linear models such as a fault tree and "quick fixes". Peer review of the causal analysis is suggested. A system description of the organisation supports both causal and hazard analyses.

### 2.7 Immediate reaction and occurrence reporting (CAMO.A.155, CAMO.A.160)
- **Implement:** safety measures mandated by the authority (CAMO.B.135) and EASA mandatory safety information (e.g. ADs and EASA safety directives).
- **Occurrence reporting system** per Reg. 376/2014 and 2015/1018, as part of the management system.
- **Report to the competent authority AND to the organisation responsible for the design of the aircraft:** any incident, malfunction, technical defect, exceeding of technical limitations, occurrence showing inaccurate, incomplete or ambiguous Part 21 (or Part 21 Light) data, or other irregular circumstance that has or may have endangered safe operation, and has not resulted in an accident or serious incident.
- Reports use the authority's form and manner and contain all pertinent information known.
- **Timing: as soon as possible, and in any case within 72 hours** of the organisation identifying the condition, unless exceptional circumstances prevent this.
- **Follow-up report**, where relevant, giving preventive actions as soon as they are identified.
- AMC1:
  - With multiple certificates, an integrated reporting system is allowed.
  - Single reports are allowed only if they include all relevant perspectives, address all mandatory data fields, identify all certificate holders concerned, and the same authority covers all certificates and has agreed.
  - Assign one or more qualified persons to coordinate airworthiness occurrence actions and investigations. If several, designate a **single focal point** with a single reporting channel to the accountable manager.
- AMC2 (ED 2023/013): share relevant safety occurrence reports with the design approval holder (DAH) or the declarant of a declaration of design compliance, and liaise on service information. UK? (declarant wording comes from Part 21 Light)
- GM1: the 2015/1018 list is **not exhaustive**. See AMC 20-8.
- GM1 CAMO.A.160(b): the "organisation responsible for the design" is the holder of a TC, restricted TC, STC, ETSO authorisation, repair or change approval, or other approval or declaration.

### 2.8 Management system and safety management (CAMO.A.200 + AMC/GM)
- **CAMO.A.200(a): the system must include**
  1. clearly defined lines of responsibility and accountability, including the **direct safety accountability of the accountable manager**;
  2. a safety policy;
  3. hazard identification, risk evaluation and management, mitigation, and verification of effectiveness;
  4. trained and competent personnel;
  5. documentation of all key processes, including a process to make personnel aware of their responsibilities and a documentation amendment procedure;
  6. a **compliance monitoring function** with a feedback system of findings to the accountable manager;
  7. any additional requirements.
- (b) Proportionate to size, nature, complexity and risks.
- (c) May be integrated with other certificates under 2018/1139.
- (d) For licensed air carriers it must be integrated with the operator's management system.
- (e) Under M.A.201(ea) it must be harmonised with the business grouping operators' systems. UK?
- **GM1 CAMO.A.200:**
  - The framework (CAMO.A.200, .202, .205) covers the ICAO Annex 19 Appendix 2 SMS core elements.
  - Compared with the old Part-M Subpart G quality system, the new elements are the safety policy and objectives, just-culture safety reporting, and hazard identification and risk management.
  - **Key safety management processes:** hazard identification; safety risk management; internal investigation; safety performance monitoring and measurement; management of change; continuous improvement; immediate safety action and coordination with the operator's ERP.
  - Compliance monitoring outputs feed risk management, and risk management sets the focus areas for compliance monitoring.
- **AMC1 CAMO.A.200(a)(1): organisation**
  - A **safety manager** and a **safety review board (SRB)** are included in the structure.
  - The SRB is a high-level committee chaired by the **accountable manager**, made up of the persons nominated under CAMO.A.305(a) and (b).
  - The SRB monitors safety performance against the policy and objectives, the timeliness of safety actions, and the effectiveness of processes. It may also review compliance monitoring results and corrective and preventive action implementation. It ensures resources are allocated.
  - The safety manager (or a designee) may attend SRB meetings.
  - Small organisations may omit a formal SRB, subject to a risk assessment and authority agreement. The SRB tasks then go to the safety manager.
- **GM1 (a)(1): safety action group (SAG)**
  - Optional, standing or ad hoc, possibly several. It reports to the SRB.
  - Tasks: monitor safety performance, define risk controls, assess the impact of organisational change, ensure timely safety actions, and review the effectiveness of safety actions and promotion.
- **GM2 (a)(1):** accountability cannot be delegated; responsibility can be delegated.
- **AMC1 (a)(2): safety policy**
  - Content: commitment to safety and a positive safety culture; internal reporting principles encouraging reports of CAW errors, incidents and hazards; cooperation with compliance monitoring and investigations.
  - Endorsed by the accountable manager, communicated with visible endorsement, and periodically reviewed.
  - Commitments: comply with legislation and improve; provide resources; apply HF principles; safety as a primary responsibility of all managers; **just culture** (do not use occurrence information to blame front-line staff for actions commensurate with their experience and training, or for any non-safety purpose).
  - **Safety objectives** form the basis of safety performance monitoring, reflect continuous improvement, are communicated, and are periodically reviewed.
  - GM1: just culture principles come from Reg. 376/2014 Art. 16(11).
- **AMC1 (a)(3): key processes**
  - (a) **Hazard identification:** a reporting scheme for reactive events and proactive hazards (collect, record, analyse, act, give feedback). Include HF hazards and hazards from organisational set-up or complex contracting and subcontracting chains.
  - (b) **Risk management:** analysis (probability and severity), assessment (tolerability), and control (mitigation) to an acceptable level. Specify the management levels that have authority to decide risk tolerability.
  - (c) **Internal investigation:** of errors and near misses under just culture. The scope goes beyond CAMO.A.160 reportables to include CAMO.A.202(b) internal reports.
  - (d) **Safety performance monitoring and measurement:** against policy and objectives. May include safety reporting (including compliance status), safety reviews and trend reviews (on new products, equipment, procedures or organisational change), safety audits, and safety surveys.
  - (e) **Management of change:** a documented process to identify external and internal changes with adverse safety effect, using the existing hazard and risk processes.
  - (f) **Continuous improvement:** via external audits, assessments (including of safety culture and SRM effectiveness), staff and cultural surveys, monitoring the recurrence of incidents, SPI evaluation, and lessons learnt.
  - (g) **Immediate safety action:** a procedure to act promptly on concerns with immediate flight safety effect, with clear instructions on who to contact at the owner or operator and how, **including outside normal business hours**. If applicable, a procedure to support the operator's **ERP** when it is triggered.
- **GM1 (a)(3): interfaces in complex arrangements**
  - Identify all parties, including independent experts and non-approved organisations.
  - Assess across all subcontract levels: coordination and interfaces, procedures, communication and reporting channels, task allocation and authorities, and key personnel qualifications.
  - Aim for one party responsible per aspect with no overlaps, clear reporting lines, and the ability of staff to notify the organisation directly of an obviously unacceptable risk.
  - Hold regular communication among the parties.
- **GM2 (a)(3): management of change**
  - Any change, large or small, triggers hazard identification and risk management.
  - Examples: organisational structure; a new aircraft type in the terms of approval; more aircraft of the same or similar type; significant personnel changes or high turnover; new or amended regulations; security arrangements; economic or financial pressure; new schedules, locations, equipment or procedures; new subcontractors.
  - Consider HF impact (including computer system changes) and the transition period.
  - Use formal hazard identification and risk assessment for major changes and changes in key personnel.
  - Review previous risk assessments.
- **AMC1 (a)(4): safety communication**
  - Ensure awareness of SMS activities, convey safety-critical information, and explain why actions are taken or procedures changed. Regular staff meetings are one means.
  - GM1: safety promotion = training + communication + information sharing.
- **GM1 (a)(5): documentation**
  - The policy, objectives and key processes can be in a separate Safety Management Manual or Management System Manual, or in CAME Part 2.
  - Separately kept documents must be referenced and are integral to the management system documentation.

### 2.9 Compliance monitoring (AMC1 to AMC4 CAMO.A.200(a)(6), GM)
- **Independence:** audits and inspections are done by personnel **not responsible for** the functions, procedures or products audited.
- **Independent audit:**
  - Routine sample checks of all aspects, including some **product sampling**.
  - An **audit plan** shows when and how often Part-M, Part-ML and Part-CAMO activities are audited.
  - **All aspects of Part-CAMO compliance are verified every year (12 months), including all subcontracted activities.** This can be one exercise or spread over the year.
  - A common procedure does not need checking against each product line if it has been verified yearly without findings. Where findings exist, check it against other product lines until the findings are closed.
- **Extension:** with no safety-related findings, the audit planning cycle may be increased by **up to 100%** (i.e. up to 24 months), subject to a risk assessment and/or mitigation and authority agreement.
- **Multiple approved locations:** each location is audited every year, or at a risk-assessed interval agreed by the authority that does not exceed the applicable audit planning cycle.
- **An audit report is issued for each audit:** what was checked and the non-compliance findings.
- **Contracted auditors:** they work under the compliance monitoring manager's responsibility. The organisation ensures their knowledge and experience, including in compliance monitoring, and retains ultimate responsibility, especially for corrective action follow-up.
- **Feedback system:**
  - It must **not be contracted out**.
  - For each non-compliance: root cause(s) and contributing factors, and corrective actions defined. Define who addresses it and the escalation procedure if the corrective action is overdue.
  - Audit reports go to the relevant departments with **target closure dates** agreed with them before confirmation. The departments implement and report status back.
  - Unless the SRB reviews compliance monitoring results, the accountable manager holds regular progress meetings. These can be delegated day to day to the compliance monitoring manager, but the accountable manager meets senior staff **at least twice per year** and receives **at least a half-yearly summary report** of non-compliance findings.
  - Audit and feedback records are kept for the CAMO.A.220(b) period (5 years) or as long as needed to support changes to the audit planning cycle, **whichever is longer**.
- GM1: the compliance monitoring function itself is subject to independent compliance monitoring.
- GM1 (a)(6) and CAMO.B.300: remote audits using ICT follow GM1 145.A.200(a)(6) and 145.B.300 (not reproduced).

### 2.10 Integration and harmonisation (GM1 CAMO.A.200(e)) [ED 2022/017, UK?]
- A "management system" is a set of interrelated organisation policies, procedures, standards and processes under an overarching safety culture.
- An integrated system (AOC + CAMO) is linked to the operator's accountable manager's corporate authority, possibly with a common SMM.
- Harmonisation in a business grouping uses common standards and needs continuous exchange of hazard, risk, decision, action, compliance and best-practice information.
- An M.A.201(ea) CAMO serves at least 2 operators, which are then harmonised with each other.

### 2.11 Information security (CAMO.A.200A)
- An ISMS per Reg. 2023/203, in addition to the management system, to manage information security risks that may affect aviation safety. **Applicable from 22 February 2026.** UK? Likely not retained; the UK has its own cyber oversight approach (guess).

### 2.12 Internal safety reporting scheme (CAMO.A.202 + AMC/GM)
- Collects and evaluates CAMO.A.160 occurrences **and** internally reported errors, near misses and hazards.
- Identifies causes and contributing factors and addresses them through SRM. Evaluates all known information, including inability to follow procedures, and circulates it.
- **Access must be given to any subcontracted organisation.**
- Cooperate on safety investigations with organisations contributing significantly to the CAMO's safety.
- AMC1 elements:
  - **confidential**, encouraging free and frank reporting;
  - aims and objectives with corporate commitment;
  - a just culture policy and implementation procedures;
  - a process to select reports for investigation, investigate all causal factors (technical, organisational, managerial, HF), and analyse trends where proportionate;
  - corrective actions;
  - initial and recurrent training for investigators;
  - cooperation with the owner or operator on investigations.
  It must ensure reporter confidentiality, be **closed-loop**, and feed recurrent training. Feedback goes to staff individually and generally.
- GM1:
  - The purpose is not blame.
  - Objectives: assess the safety implications of each report, including previous similar issues, and share knowledge.
  - It complements day-to-day controls.
  - **"All reports should be retained"**, as their significance may only become obvious later.

### 2.13 Facilities (CAMO.A.215, AMC1)
- Suitable offices for CAW management, planning, technical records and management system staff.
- One shared office is possible with authority agreement if there is space and no undue disturbance.
- Include an **adequate technical library** and room for document consultation.

### 2.14 Personnel (CAMO.A.305 + AMC/GM)
**Accountable manager (AM) (a):**
- Has corporate authority to ensure all CAW management activities can be financed and carried out. The AM must:
  1. ensure the necessary resources;
  2. establish and promote the safety policy;
  3. nominate person(s) responsible for compliance with CAW management, airworthiness review and permit to fly requirements, i.e. the **CAW nominated person(s)** under (a)(3);
  4. nominate person(s) to manage the **compliance monitoring function** under (a)(4);
  5. nominate person(s) to manage **safety management** processes under (a)(5);
  6. ensure those nominated persons, and the (b)(2) post holder, have **direct access** to the AM;
  7. demonstrate a basic understanding of the Regulation.
- AMC1 (a):
  - Normally the CEO, with overall and financial responsibility.
  - May be the AM for more than one organisation and need not be technical.
  - If not the CEO, the organisation must show the AM has direct access to the CEO and the necessary funding allocation.
- The AM signs the CAME statement, which the CEO countersigns if the AM is not the CEO. A **new AM signs at the earliest opportunity**.

**Licensed air carriers (b):**
- (b)(1) The AM is the same person as the air carrier AM under ORO.GEN.210(a).
- (b)(2) The AM nominates a **post holder** for management and supervision of CAW. The post holder must **not be employed by a Part-145 organisation under contract to the operator**, unless the authority specifically agrees.
- AMC1 (b)(2): if nominating a Part-145-employed post holder, the carrier must justify it with a risk assessment and/or mitigation. This applies only to contracted maintenance, not where the 145 organisation and the carrier are the same organisation.
- (ba) Under an M.A.201(ea) contract, the (a)(3) persons must not be employed by a Part-145 organisation under contract to the CAMO, unless agreed. UK?
- GM1 (b): business grouping operators and the CAMO, if not the same legal entity, need not share an AM. UK?

**Nominated persons (c), AMC1 CAMO.A.305(c):**
- They must demonstrate relevant knowledge, background, satisfactory CAW experience and a working knowledge of the Regulation, and are ultimately responsible to the AM.
- AMC1 recommended profile for the CAMO.A.305(a) and (b) nominees:
  - (a) practical experience applying aviation safety standards;
  - (b) comprehensive knowledge of operational requirements, the AOC ops specs and the operations manual, where applicable;
  - (c) knowledge of HF principles and SMS (EU requirements including compliance monitoring, ICAO Annex 19);
  - (d) **5 years' relevant work experience, of which at least 2 years in the aeronautical industry in an appropriate position**;
  - (e) a **relevant engineering degree** (aeronautical, mechanical, electrical, electronic, avionics or similar) or an aircraft maintenance technician qualification with additional education acceptable to the authority. This can be replaced by **5 years of experience in addition** to (d), i.e. 10 in total, covering maintenance, CAW management or surveillance. For a (a)(4) or (a)(5) nominee who already holds an equivalent post (CMM or SM) under another certificate, (e) can be replaced by a specific training programme acceptable to the authority;
  - (f) thorough knowledge of the CAME;
  - (g) type knowledge of a **relevant sample** of the types in scope, via a formal course at least equivalent to **Part-66 Appendix III Level 1 General Familiarisation** (from a Part-147, the manufacturer or another accepted organisation). For **balloons and any aircraft of 2 730 kg MTOM or less**, documented evidence or a recorded authority assessment may replace the course;
  - (h) knowledge of maintenance methods;
  - (i) knowledge of the applicable regulations.
- AMC1 (a)(3): the CAW nominated person(s) represent the management structure and are responsible for daily operation of all CAW functions. Functions may be split or combined.
- GM1 (a)(3): they ensure day-to-day compliance, have a complete understanding of the requirements, and proactively manage compliance, documenting and acting on early warning signs.

**Safety manager and compliance monitoring manager, AMC1 CAMO.A.305(a)(4);(a)(5):**
- If several persons share safety management, the AM identifies a single focal point, the **"safety manager"**. Functions:
  - facilitate hazard identification, risk assessment and management;
  - monitor implementation of the safety action plan, unless compliance monitoring follows it up;
  - give periodic safety performance reports to the SRB;
  - maintain safety management documentation;
  - ensure acceptable safety training is available;
  - advise on safety;
  - ensure internal occurrence investigations are started and followed up.
- If several persons share compliance monitoring, the AM identifies the **"compliance monitoring manager" (CMM)**. Role:
  - ensure activities are monitored for compliance under the nominated persons' supervision;
  - monitor contracted maintenance against the contract or work order;
  - implement, maintain and improve the audit plan;
  - request corrections and corrective actions.
- The CMM must **not be one of the CAMO.A.305(a)(3) persons**, must have compliance monitoring knowledge and experience, and must have access to all parts of the organisation and subcontractors.
- Combined duties must not cause conflicts of interest. **Compliance monitoring must be independent of CAW management functions.**
- If the same person is both CMM and SM, the AM ensures sufficient resources for both.
- Small organisations: the CMM and/or SM role may be exercised by the **AM**, subject to a risk assessment and/or mitigation and authority agreement, provided the AM has demonstrated the competency in (b)(2)(ii).
- GM1 (a)(5): the SM may be assisted by safety staff but stays the unique focal point.
- GM3 (g) **safety manager competency:** ICAO and EU SMS knowledge; management systems including compliance monitoring; risk management; investigation and root cause techniques; HF; safety culture promotion; operational experience; safety management experience; interpersonal and leadership skills; oral and written communication; data management, analysis and problem solving.

**Staffing (d), AMC1 (d):**
- A system to plan staff availability so there are enough qualified staff to plan, perform, supervise, inspect and monitor activities.
- No formula. The headcount depends on fleet size and type, complexity, age, CAT network, ETOPS and contracting.
- Make a **task analysis**: tasks, how they are divided or combined, responsibilities, **man-hours** and qualifications. Keep it up to date and review it on significant change.
- Have a procedure to assess and mitigate risk when actual staff is below plan for a shift or period, and when the proportion of contracted staff temporarily increases.

**ARS and ARC extension staff (e), (f):**
- (e) AR, recommendation and PtF privileges require ARS qualified and authorised per CAMO.A.310.
- (f) For ARC extension under (d)(4), nominate the authorised persons.
- GM1 (f): approval of the CAME listing these persons (CAMO.A.300(a)(5)) is both authority acceptance and organisation authorisation. ARS are automatically recognised as able to extend ARCs.

**Competency control (g):**
- Applies to personnel in compliance monitoring, safety management, CAW management, ARs and recommendations, and PtF issue. Follow a procedure and standard agreed by the authority. Competency must include an understanding of SMS and HF appropriate to the function. Changing the procedure needs prior approval.
- AMC1 (g):
  - Assess technical support staff (planners, engineers, technical records), supervisors, post holders and ARS, whether **employed or contracted**, **before unsupervised work starts**, and control competency continuously.
  - Assessment means: on-the-job performance and/or knowledge testing by qualified personnel; training records (basic, organisational, type and differences); experience records. Validation may include a check with the issuing organisation. A log book may be used.
  - The outcome sets the supervision level, whether unsupervised work is allowed, and any training need.
  - Keep a record of each individual's qualifications and competency assessment, including copies of qualification documents and authorisations.
  - Provide and record initial and recurrent training. All staff show knowledge of CAMO procedures and an understanding of SMS and HF.
  - **Job descriptions** are recommended for each job function, with assessment criteria.
  - Criteria by role: managers; AMP engineers (interpret source data to develop the AMP); engineering staff (interpret data, e.g. make work cards); planners; compliance monitoring staff; safety staff; all staff (safety policy and reporting tools); M.A.201(ea) common language skills (e.g. English).
- AMC2 (g) **procedure contents:**
  1. who is responsible;
  2. when assessment happens;
  3. credit from previous assessments;
  4. validation of qualification records;
  5. initial assessment methods;
  6. continuous control methods, including performance feedback;
  7. competencies to observe per job function;
  8. actions if the assessment is unsatisfactory;
  9. how results are recorded.
  Assessment may be by supervised work "for a sufficient time", possibly as little as a few weeks. Written confirmation from a previous approved CAMO is acceptable. All prospective CAW staff are assessed.
- AMC3 (g) **safety training (including HF):**
  - Assess everyone for the need for initial safety training.
  - **Initial and recurrent** safety training is required for at least: nominated persons and line managers; compliance monitoring and safety management staff (including HF, investigations and training); **ARS**; planners, engineers and technical records staff; AMP and reliability staff; contract staff in these categories.
  - **Initial training within 6 months of joining.** Temporary staff may need it sooner. Recruits from elsewhere and temporary staff are assessed for additional training.
  - Initial training covers the full GM2 syllabus, which can be adjusted per organisation or function.
  - **Recurrent training of appropriate duration in each 2-year period**, tailored to audit findings and safety and HF information.
  - Trainers formally report feedback through the internal safety reporting scheme.
  - Training may be delivered in-house, by independent trainers, or by acceptable training organisations.
- AMC4 (g) **other training:**
  - Assess needs for EWIS (AMC 20-22), Continuing Structural Integrity (AMC 20-20) and CDCCL.
  - Fuel tank safety training per Appendix III.
  - CMM training: requirements, manuals, audit techniques, reporting and recording.
  - AMP and reliability staff: statistical analysis, reliability methods, and MSG logic.
- AMC5 (g): adequate initial and recurrent training, recorded. Recurrent training uses information from the internal safety reporting scheme.
- GM1 (g): safety training is needed at initial SMS implementation, for new staff or those newly given safety tasks, regularly as refreshers, when personnel changes affect safety roles, and for dedicated safety functions. It is subject to CAMO.A.220(c) record-keeping.
- GM2 (g): initial safety training syllabus. See Section 7.

### 2.15 Airworthiness review staff (ARS) (CAMO.A.310 + AMC)
- **Qualifications (a):** ARS issuing ARCs or recommendations, and PtFs if applicable, must have:
  1. **at least 5 years' experience in continuing airworthiness**;
  2. an appropriate **Part-66 licence**, an **aeronautical degree** or a national equivalent;
  3. **formal aeronautical maintenance training**;
  4. a **position with appropriate responsibilities** in the approved organisation.
- (b) (a)(2) can be replaced by **5 additional years** of CAW experience, i.e. 10 years in total.
- (c) An authorisation is issued only after **formal acceptance by the authority** following a satisfactory **airworthiness review under supervision** of the authority, or of the organisation's authorised ARS, per a CAME procedure approved by the authority.
- (d) Recent experience: ARS must show appropriate recent CAW management experience.
- AMC1 (a):
  - ARS are needed only for the (e) and (f) privileges.
  - "Experience in continuing airworthiness" means any appropriate combination of experience in aircraft maintenance, CAW management and/or surveillance of such tasks.
  - A person meeting AMC1 CAMO.A.305(c)(e) is treated as holding the equivalent of an aeronautical degree.
  - **Appropriate Part-66 licence:** B1 or L licence in the subcategory of the aircraft reviewed; or B2 or C; or for **piston-engine non-pressurised aeroplanes of 2 000 kg MTOM and below**, B3. Part-66 experience requirements need not be met at the time of the review.
  - **Appropriate position** means independent of the airworthiness management process, or having overall authority over the CAW management of complete aircraft.
    - Independence can be achieved by: reviewing only aircraft the person did not manage (e.g. a different type); MO staff of a CAMO that also holds an MO approval who are not involved in managing that aircraft and **did not release it to service** (except maintenance during or arising from the physical survey); or compliance monitoring department staff.
    - Overall authority can be achieved by: the AM or the nominated post holder; or reviewing only aircraft for which the person is responsible for the complete CAW process. In one-man organisations the person always has overall authority.
- AMC1 (a)(3) **formal aeronautical maintenance training**, with evidence, on: initial and continuing airworthiness regulations; operational requirements if applicable; the organisation's CAME; a relevant type sample (at least Part-66 Appendix III Level 1 General Familiarisation from a Part-147, the manufacturer or an accepted organisation); and maintenance methods.
- AMC1 (c): approval of the CAME containing the **nominative list** of ARS (CAMO.A.300(a)(8)) is the formal authority acceptance and also the organisation's authorisation. If the supervised review was done under existing ARS, evidence goes to the authority.
- **AMC1 (d) recency and validity.** To keep the authorisation valid the ARS must have **either**:
  - been involved in CAW management activities for **at least 6 months in every 2-year period**, **or**
  - conducted **at least one airworthiness review in the last 12-month period**.
  To **restore** validity: conduct a satisfactory airworthiness review under supervision of the authority or, if the authority accepts, of another currently authorised ARS of the same CAMO, per an approved procedure.

### 2.16 Continuing airworthiness management tasks (CAMO.A.315 + AMC/GM)
- (a) All CAW management follows Part-M Section A Subpart C or Part-ML Section A Subpart C.
- (b) **For every aircraft managed:**
  1. develop and control the **AMP**, including any reliability programme (M.A.302 / ML.A.302);
  2. for aircraft not used by licensed air carriers, give a **copy of the AMP** to the responsible owner or operator;
  3. ensure **modification and repair data** complies with M.A.304 / ML.A.304;
  4. for all **complex motor-powered aircraft (CMPA)** or licensed air carrier aircraft, have a procedure to **assess non-mandatory modifications and/or inspections** and decide on their application using SRM;
  5. take the aircraft, engines, propellers and components to an appropriately approved MO (Part-M Subpart F, Part-145 or Part-CAO) whenever necessary;
  6. **order maintenance, supervise, and coordinate decisions** so maintenance is done properly and appropriately released.
- (c) If the CAMO is not itself an approved MO, it manages the written maintenance contracts required by M.A.201(e)(3), (f)(3), (g)(3), (h)(3) or ML.A.201, in consultation with the operator. The contracts must ensure all maintenance is ultimately done by an approved MO, and the M.A.301(b), (c), (f), (g) / ML.A.301 functions are clearly specified.
- (d) **Work orders instead of a contract** are allowed for unscheduled line maintenance and for component maintenance, including engines and propellers.
- (e) HF and human performance limitations are considered in all CAW management, including contracted and subcontracted work.
- AMC1 CAMO.A.315:
  - Adequate knowledge of the design and configuration: type specification, customer options, ADs, ICA airworthiness limitations, mods, repairs, operational and emergency equipment, and required and performed maintenance. Configuration and maintenance status must be adequately documented.
  - For CS-25 aeroplanes: CS-25 Book 1 Appendix H para H25.4 limitations and fuel tank system limitations including **CDCCL**.
- GM1 (b)(1): "control" of the AMP means approving the AMP and its amendments for **Part-ML** aircraft. For **Part-M** aircraft it means presenting it to the authority for approval, unless covered by the **indirect approval** procedure (M.A.302(c)).
- AMC1 (b)(3): take CDCCL into account when managing mod and repair approvals.
- AMC1 (b)(4): a policy to assess non-mandatory information: SBs, service letters and other information from the design organisation, manufacturer, authority or EASA.
- GM1 (b)(5): the CAMO decides **what maintenance, when, by whom and to what standard**.
- AMC1 (c) (ED 2023/013):
  - Tasks are Part-M M.A.301 (b), (c), (e), (f), (g), (h) and Part-ML ML.A.301 (b), (c), (d), (e). Without an MO approval, contract the appropriate organisations.
  - The CAMO is responsible for the airworthy condition of the aircraft and must be **satisfied before the intended flight that all required maintenance has been properly carried out**.
  - Agree the MO selection process with the operator before contracting.
  - The CAMO may check contracted work at the MO facilities.
  - The contract details each party's responsibilities and work, clearly and unambiguously.
  - Pay special attention to: all maintenance done; SBs analysed and decisions taken; ADs done on time; all work, including non-mandatory mods, done to approved data or data declared under Part 21 Light Subpart C, and to the latest standards. UK? (the "declared" wording is Part 21 Light)
  - Appendix IV gives more detail.
- AMC2 (c):
  - A maintenance contract with a **secondary operator/CAMO** without an MO approval is acceptable if it simplifies management and the CAMO keeps control.
  - The CAME then needs procedures to ensure all maintenance is ultimately done on time by approved MOs to appropriate data. Compliance monitoring and SRM must emphasise this.
  - The list of approved MOs, or a reference to it, is in the CAME.
  - Typical cases: a primary contractor dispatching components to Part-145 shops; dry-lease continuity, keeping the lessor's maintenance arrangements via a single contract.
  - The same level of control applies through the (a) nominated persons and the management system.
- GM1 (c): for line maintenance the **IATA Standard Ground Handling Agreement** layout may be used, provided the contract allows the CAMO to exercise its responsibility.
- GM1 (d): work orders are acceptable when the CAME allows one-time orders for unscheduled line maintenance and component maintenance up to engines, if manageable in volume and complexity. **Base maintenance needs a written contract even if ordered case by case.**

### 2.17 Airworthiness review (CAMO.A.320)
- Performed per M.A.901 (Part-M) or ML.A.903 (Part-ML). The detailed AR process is in Part-M and Part-ML chunks, not here.

### 2.18 Maintenance data (CAMO.A.325 + AMC/GM)
- Hold and use **applicable current** maintenance data (M.A.401 / ML.A.401) for CAMO.A.315 tasks.
- Data may come from the owner or operator under a contract. It is then kept only for the contract's duration, unless it is a record under CAMO.A.220(a).
- AMC1: when using customer-provided data, the CAMO ensures it is current, through procedures or contract provisions.
- GM1: customer data used for CAW activities that counts as a record under CAMO.A.220(a)(2) is kept for the CAMO.A.220(a)(5) period, i.e. 3 years after transfer.
- GM2: CAMO.A.325 covers CAW management tasks but **not airworthiness reviews**.

## 3. Records and Documents (retention and contents)

| Record / document | Source | Contents | Retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| CAW records required by M.A.305, ML.A.305 and M.A.306 (aircraft records, ATL) | CAMO.A.220(a)(1) | Per Part-M / Part-ML (other chunks) | Per M.A.305 / ML.A.305 / M.A.306 (not restated here) |
| Details of all work carried out | CAMO.A.220(a)(2) | All CAW management work done | Until **3 years after** responsibility for the aircraft (M.A.201 / ML.A.201) is **permanently transferred** to another person or organisation (a)(5) |
| ARC and recommendation copies, including extensions, with **all supporting documents** | CAMO.A.220(a)(3) | Each ARC or recommendation issued or extended under (e). Also a copy of any ARC extended under (d)(4) | 3 years after permanent transfer (a)(5) |
| Permit to fly copies | CAMO.A.220(a)(4) | Each PtF issued per 21.A.729 | 3 years after permanent transfer (a)(5) |
| All retained records on termination of operations | CAMO.A.220(a)(6) | n/a | **Transfer to the aircraft owner** |
| Records kept on the CAMO's behalf by an MO | AMC2 CAMO.A.220(b) | n/a | The CAMO stays responsible, and must transfer them to the next CAW manager when it ceases to be the CAMO |
| Complete CRS | AMC2 CAMO.A.220(a) | CRS from the approved MO, independent certifying staff (M.A.801(b)(1), ML.A.801(b)(2)) or the pilot-owner | The CAMO must always receive a complete CRS. The record system is described in the CAME |
| Management system key process records | CAMO.A.220(b)(1)(i) | Hazard log, risk assessments, investigations, SPIs, MoC, audits, findings, training, etc. | **Minimum 5 years** (b)(2) |
| Contracts (maintenance contracting and CAW subcontracting) | CAMO.A.220(b)(1)(ii) | Per CAMO.A.205 | **Minimum 5 years** |
| Independent audit and feedback records | AMC4 CAMO.A.200(a)(6)(f) | Audit reports, findings, CAPs, closure | 5 years **or** as long as needed to support audit planning cycle changes, **whichever is longer** |
| Internal safety reports | GM1 CAMO.A.202(d) | All reports | "All reports should be retained" (no limit given; at least the 5-year management system period) |
| Personnel records: CAW management, compliance monitoring and safety management staff | CAMO.A.220(c)(1)(i) | Qualification and experience | While employed **plus 3 years** after leaving (c)(3) |
| Personnel records: ARS, recommendation staff, PtF staff | CAMO.A.220(c)(1)(ii), (c)(2) | Qualifications held, summary of relevant CAW management experience and training, **copy of the authorisation** | While employed plus 3 years |
| ARS minimum record | AMC1 CAMO.A.220(c)(1)(ii) | Name; date of birth; basic education; experience; aeronautical degree and/or Part-66 and/or national qualification; initial training; type of training; recurrent training; experience in CAW and within the organisation; responsibilities of current role; copy of the authorisation | While employed plus 3 years |
| Competency assessment records | AMC1 CAMO.A.305(g) | Each individual's qualifications and competency assessment, copies of documents attesting qualifications and authorisations | Personnel records rule (plus 3 years) |
| Safety training records | GM1 CAMO.A.305(g)(c) | Initial and recurrent | CAMO.A.220(c) |
| Nominated person type-knowledge assessment (≤ 2 730 kg / balloons) | AMC1 CAMO.A.305(c)(g) | Authority assessment "should be recorded" | Personnel records |
| Staffing task analysis (man-hours) | AMC1 CAMO.A.305(d) | Tasks, division, responsibilities, man-hours, qualifications | Keep current. Review on significant change |
| Customer-provided maintenance data | CAMO.A.325, GM1 | Data used | Contract duration, or (a)(5) if it is a record |
| CAME, plus associated manuals | CAMO.A.300 | See below | Controlled document, kept up to date |
| Default rule | AMC1 CAMO.A.220(d) | Any record with no specified period | **Minimum 3 years** |

**General record-keeping rules (CAMO.A.220(d) to (f), AMC1/GM1):**
- Adequate storage and reliable traceability. Format specified in procedures. Protection from damage, alteration and theft.
- Accessible within a reasonable time, traceable and retrievable for the whole retention period.
- Paper, electronic, microfilm or optical disc are all acceptable, and must stay legible.
- **The retention period starts when the record is created or last amended.**
- Computer systems: **at least one backup, updated within 24 hours of any new entry**; safeguards against unauthorised alteration; backup hardware stored in a **different location** from the working data, in a suitable environment.
- Data must stay accessible through hardware and software changes.
- Microfilm or optical copies may be made at any time and must be as legible as the original.

**CAME contents (CAMO.A.300(a)):**
1. AM statement, countersigned by the CEO if different;
2. safety policy;
3. scope of work;
4. manpower resources and staff planning system;
5. titles and names of the (a)(3) to (a)(5), (b)(2) and (f) persons;
6. duties, accountabilities, responsibilities and authorities of the (a)(3) to (a)(5), (b)(2), (e) and (f) persons;
7. organisation chart of the chains of accountability;
8. **list of staff authorised to issue ARCs or recommendations, and PtF signatories** (the source text says "point (c) of CAMO.A.125"; this appears to be a typo for (f));
9. facilities: description and location;
10. internal safety reporting scheme;
11. procedures: (i) management system key processes; (ii) control of contracted and subcontracted activities; (iii) CAW management, AR and PtF procedures; (iv) the procedure for changes not requiring prior approval; (v) CAME amendment procedures;
12. list of approved AMPs for contracted aircraft;
13. list of maintenance contracts (CAMO.A.315(c));
14. list of currently approved AltMoCs.
- (b) The initial issue is approved by the authority and amended as needed to stay up to date.
- (c) Amendments follow procedures (a)(11)(iv) and (v). Amendments outside the (iv) scope, and those related to CAMO.A.130(a) changes, need authority approval.
- AMC1 CAMO.A.300 model layout: see Section 7.
- AMC2:
  - Staff are familiar with the CAME parts relevant to them.
  - **Designate the person responsible for monitoring and amending the CAME** and associated manuals.
  - EDP publication is allowed if compatible with internal and external dissemination.
- AMC3: for a business grouping, the CAME covers operator-specific requirements. UK?

## 4. Defined Terms (GM1 to Annex Vc, plus terms defined elsewhere in the chunk)

- **Audit:** "a systematic, independent, and documented process for obtaining evidence, and evaluating it objectively to determine the extent to which requirements are complied with". It may include inspections.
- **Alternative means of compliance (AltMoC):** means proposing an alternative to an existing AMC, or new means where no AMC exists.
- **Assessment:** in performance monitoring and oversight, a planned, documented evaluation by competent personnel of the level of performance and maturity against policy and objectives. It looks at the whole organisation to find strengths and weaknesses. Distinct from risk assessment.
- **Base maintenance / Line maintenance:** see AMC1 145.A.10 (not here).
- **Competency:** "a combination of individual skills, practical and theoretical knowledge, attitudes, training, and experience".
- **Correction:** "the action to eliminate a detected non-compliance".
- **Corrective action:** the action to eliminate or mitigate the root cause(s) and prevent recurrence of an existing detected non-compliance or undesirable condition. Proper root cause determination is crucial.
- **Error:** an action or inaction by a person that may lead to deviations from accepted procedures or regulations.
- **Hazard:** "a condition or an object with the potential to cause or contribute to an aircraft incident or accident".
- **Human factors:** anything that affects human performance; principles seeking a safe interface between the human and other system components.
- **Human performance:** human capabilities and limitations affecting safety and efficiency.
- **Inspection:** in compliance monitoring, an independent documented conformity evaluation by observation and judgement, with measurement or testing as appropriate. May be part of an audit (e.g. product audit) or stand alone (e.g. to verify closure of a finding).
- **Just Culture:** see Reg. 376/2014 Art. 2.
- **Near-miss:** an event in which a mandatorily reportable occurrence (376/2014) was narrowly averted. Example: CAMO staff find on recheck that an AD, AWL or CMR task was not properly processed in the AMP or record system, which would have led to it not being done on time.
- **Organisational factor:** a condition affecting the effectiveness of safety risk controls, related to culture, policies, processes, resources or workplace.
- **Oversight planning cycle:** the time frame within which the authority reviews all areas and processes of the approval by audits and inspections.
- **Oversight programme:** the authority's detailed schedule: number, scope and duration of audits and inspections, product audits, locations and tentative timing.
- **Post holder:** the person nominated under CAMO.A.305(b)(2), i.e. the air carrier's CAW manager.
- **Preventive action:** the action to eliminate the cause of a **potential** non-compliance or undesirable situation.
- **Risk assessment:** an evaluation by engineering and operational judgement and/or analysis to establish whether the achieved or perceived risk is acceptable or tolerable.
- **Safety Culture:** an enduring set of values, norms, attitudes and practices concerned with minimising exposure to hazards. A positive culture promotes shared concern, commitment and accountability.
- **Safety risk:** "the predicted probability and severity of the consequences or outcomes of a hazard".
- **Safety training:** dedicated training supporting safety management policies and processes, including HF training. Safety *management* training is for staff in CAMO.A.305(a)(5) or CAMO.A.200(a)(3) functions.
- **Working days:** "days between and including Monday to Friday not including public holidays".

Other terms defined in the AMC/GM:
- **Accountability vs responsibility** (GM2 CAMO.A.200(a)(1)): accountability cannot be delegated; responsibility can.
- **Line managers** (AMC3 CAMO.A.305(g)): departmental heads or persons responsible for operational units directly delivering the basic CAW management services.
- **Authority** in the safety management context (GM1 CAMO.A.305(g)): the management level needed to decide risk tolerability.
- **Relevant engineering degree** (AMC1 CAMO.A.305(c)): aeronautical, mechanical, electrical, electronic, avionics or other studies relevant to maintenance or CAW.
- **Relevant sample** (AMC1 CAMO.A.305(c), AMC1 CAMO.A.310(a)(3)): courses covering typical aircraft and systems within the scope of work.
- **Experience in continuing airworthiness** (AMC1 CAMO.A.310(a)): any appropriate combination of maintenance, CAW management and/or surveillance of such tasks.
- **Formal aeronautical maintenance training** (AMC1 CAMO.A.310(a)(3)): see Section 2.15.
- **Management system** (GM1 CAMO.A.200(e)): see Section 2.10.
- **Integrated management system** (GM1 CAMO.A.200(e)): see Section 2.10.
- **Organisation responsible for the design** (GM1 CAMO.A.160(b)): holder of a TC, RTC, STC, ETSO authorisation, repair or change approval, or declaration.
- **Non-mandatory information** (AMC1 CAMO.A.315(b)(4)): SBs, service letters and similar from the design organisation, manufacturer, authority or EASA.
- **Safety manager / Compliance monitoring manager**: the unique focal points (AMC1 CAMO.A.305(a)(4);(a)(5)).
- **Safety review board / Safety action group**: see Section 2.8.

Abbreviations: ARS (airworthiness review staff), AMP, ARC, PtF, CMPA, CDCCL, EWIS, ERP, ATL, MEL, AltMoC, SRB, SAG, SMM, ICA, AWL, CMR, ETOPS, MSG.
